dz.headline: Hemdani names Algeria squad without Luca Zidane
dz.dek: Coach Brahim Hemdani selected 26 players for the CAN 2027 qualifiers against Togo, excluding Luca Zidane and Rayan Aït Nouri.
paragraphs: Algeria's national football team coach Brahim Hemdani announced a 26-player squad on Thursday, November 5, for two upcoming matches against Togo in the CAN 2027 qualifiers. Notably absent from the list are Luca Zidane and Rayan Aït Nouri, the latter being dropped due to a disciplinary issue during the last training camp. The squad includes two new players, Mohamed Azzi and Abderrahmane Rebbach, and recalls several players who missed the previous camp.

Hemdani explained Luca Zidane's exclusion was based on sporting criteria, specifically prioritizing goalkeepers with maximum playing time. "I made my choices on a sporting criterion, on this position which is really particular," Hemdani stated. "I needed to have a choice between three goalkeepers who had maximum playing time." Rayan Aït Nouri's absence is seen as a consequence of a past outburst, though his limited game time at Manchester City may also be a factor.

The midfield sees the return of Nabil Bentaleb and Hicham Boudaoui from injury, along with Titraoui. Abderrahmane Rebbach from Deportivo Alavés receives his first call-up, while Aouchiche and Zorgane are omitted. The attack remains largely unchanged, with Ghedjemis replacing Kebbal. The team will face Togo on November 14 and November 17.

dz.headline: Algeria opens Tindouf free trade zone
dz.dek: The 200-hectare zone near Mauritania border will boost exports to West Africa.
paragraphs: Algeria is set to open a 200-hectare free trade zone in Tindouf before the end of 2026. The zone, located near the Mauritanian border, aims to increase trade with West African nations, particularly boosting Algerian exports. Minister of Foreign Trade Kamel Rezig announced the impending operational status on Thursday, November 5.

The Tindouf free trade zone is described as a strategic project, featuring six large warehouses, exhibition spaces, a goods control center, and administrative buildings for customs, banks, and insurance. It also includes health and security services, creating a comprehensive environment for economic operators. Construction began in 2024 with the laying of the first stone by Algerian President Abdelmadjid Tebboune and Mauritanian President Mohamed Ould Cheikh El Ghazouani.

Work on the zone is now fully complete, according to Minister Rezig, who stated that final reception procedures are underway. The government is also coordinating the creation of a public establishment to manage free trade zones. This initiative is intended to establish Tindouf as a central commercial and logistics hub to enhance economic presence in Africa.

dz.headline: Algeria produces 20 million tonnes of cement surplus
dz.dek: Algeria's cement exports grew twelvefold in four years, reaching $747 million in 2023.
paragraphs: Algeria now produces nearly 20 million tonnes of cement annually as surplus, having shifted from its past import reliance. The nation's cement producers are targeting export markets across Africa, Europe, and the United States. However, ports and the new European carbon tax are hindering growth.

With an annual production capacity of approximately 41 million tonnes in 2024 and a domestic consumption of around 23 million tonnes, Algeria has a substantial exportable surplus. This excess cement is becoming a key element in the country's economic diversification strategy, contributing to non-hydrocarbon exports which reached $5.16 billion in 2025.

Cement and clinker exports have seen dramatic growth, rising from $60 million in 2019 to $747 million in 2023, a more than twelvefold increase. Algeria became the world's second-largest clinker exporter in 2023 and the top exporter in Africa and second in the Mediterranean, with France, Italy, and Belgium as key buyers.

dz.headline: Algeria shares water desalination experience in Malta
dz.dek: Algerian Water Desalination Company presented its strategy for 2025-2030, focusing on brine valorization.
paragraphs: Algeria is enhancing its water desalination industry by seeking ways to utilize waste products and convert them into valuable resources. This initiative was the focus of Algeria's participation in a regional meeting held in Malta on November 3 and 4. The Algerian Water Desalination Company, a subsidiary of Sonatrach, showcased Algeria's experience in developing desalination facilities and improving their technical, energy, and environmental performance.

The meeting provided a platform to discuss national water security efforts and address water scarcity exacerbated by climate change. The company outlined its strategic vision for 2025-2030, particularly concerning the valorization of brine, a byproduct of desalination. This involves studying the potential for extracting economic, industrial, and environmental value from brine using scientific research and innovative technologies.

To achieve this, the company is pursuing scientific and technical cooperation with national institutions, including the National Observatory for Environment and Sustainable Development and universities. This collaboration aims to develop studies on brine characteristics and explore valorization methods. The company affirmed its commitment to sustainable desalination that balances water security, industrial efficiency, technological innovation, and environmental protection, aligning with national directives and Algeria's sustainable development commitments.

dz.headline: Algeria starts potato destocking to ease market shortage
dz.dek: Potato prices have risen sharply since October 1, 2026, causing scarcity in markets.
paragraphs: Algeria has begun destocking potatoes from cold storage facilities in Aïn Defla, Médéa, Boumerdès, and Bouira provinces to address national market shortages. The commerce directorate in Ouled Djellal announced the operation on Wednesday, inviting fruit and vegetable operators to identify participating cold storage units. These reserves were initially established to regulate the market.

The scarcity follows a price cap of 80-90 Algerian dinars per kilogram for retail potatoes, implemented on October 1. Some traders are reportedly selling the tubers discreetly at much higher prices. Economist Brahim Guendouzi attributes the disappearance from stalls to the significant role of intermediaries in fresh produce distribution, stating that price controls and increased inspections have discouraged regular supply at traders' terms.

Guendouzi suggests that the government's destocking plan appears insufficient, citing a combination of factors including weak production, logistical challenges like transport and storage, and numerous intermediaries. He noted that the upcoming harvests might resolve the issue. Oued Souf, a major potato-producing region, estimates its annual output at 16 million quintals.

ao.headline: Angola's farm sector grows to 23% of GDP
ao.dek: The agricultural sector's contribution to Angola's GDP has nearly doubled in 10 years, now standing at 23%.
paragraphs: Angola's economy is undergoing a structural transformation that is reducing its reliance on external vulnerabilities, according to Minister of State for Economic Coordination José de Lima Massano.

The agricultural sector's weight in the national GDP has almost doubled over the past decade, reaching approximately 23%. The food segment now constitutes 58% of the manufacturing industry, with industrial production increasing by 66% in September compared to the same period last year, based on INE data.

Massano stated that this structural shift supports a path toward sustained disinflation, as food and non-alcoholic beverages account for 56% of Angola's consumer price index. He advocated for continued public incentives to attract investment in agriculture, manufacturing, logistics, and national production.

ao.headline: MPLA committee endorses Lourenço's re-candidacy
ao.dek: The party's central committee approved the report on candidacies for the IX Congress.
paragraphs: The MPLA's highest body between congresses met in Luanda to approve the report for the upcoming IX Congress. Two pre-candidates were excluded, leaving only the current President, João Lourenço, as the sole candidate for party leader. The meeting, presided over by Lourenço himself, also approved the report from the preparatory commission regarding candidacies.

The Central Committee expressed its recognition and support for Lourenço's leadership, highlighting his efforts in consolidating party unity and addressing political and organizational challenges. The final communiqué encouraged the leader to continue with determination to overcome future challenges and congratulated him on the approval of his candidacy.

The committee's deliberations are considered important for the regular progress of the IX Ordinary Congress preparation. The final document also emphasized strengthening unity, cohesion, and political responsibility among members for the congress and the new political cycle.

ao.headline: Angolan residents decry bridge's poor state
ao.dek: Residents of Boa Esperança 2 in Kicolo are concerned about a deteriorating bridge and waste accumulation.
paragraphs: Residents of Boa Esperança 2 in Kicolo, Angola, are expressing deep concern over the deteriorating state of a local bridge, which poses daily risks, particularly for students. Barreto Pascoal, a resident, called for the communal administrator of Kicolo to engage with the community to address the infrastructure's problems.

Pascoal stated that the bridge's condition reflects broader issues in the community and that administrators must be close to the people to understand their realities. He added that the accumulation of solid waste and poor access roads worsen the difficulties faced by inhabitants.

Other residents, including Mingo Castro, emphasized the urgent need for authorities to act before a serious incident occurs, noting that people are forced to use the bridge daily despite its dangers. Cristiano Bolevo highlighted that infrastructure and sanitation issues directly impact families' quality of life.

ao.headline: Angola hosts international seminar on historical reparations
ao.dek: Mbanza Kongo will host the III International Seminar on Historical Reparations from November 9 to 14.
paragraphs: Angola will host the III International Seminar on Historical Reparations in Mbanza Kongo, Zaire province, from November 9 to 14. The event, held as Angola approaches its 51st independence anniversary on November 11, aims to position the country on the path to historical reparations.

Tânia de Carvalho, president of the Angolan Association Osoko, stated that Mbanza Kongo was chosen as the seminar's location because it was where the first slave ships arrived. The seminar, organized with the International Committee for Reparations, seeks to create a document for the African Union and the United Nations, which previously classified the slave trade as a crime against humanity.

De Carvalho explained that historical reparations for Angola should begin with Portugal recognizing the crimes committed. She noted that while many African nations are achieving progress in reparations, Angola is initiating this debate to define its process. The seminar will gather specialists, academics, politicians, and activists to conceptualize the reparations process.

ao.headline: Angola court uses insult law to silence journalists
ao.dek: Folha 8 reports that criminal insult laws are being used to suppress free expression.
paragraphs: Folha 8 reports that Angola's legal system is using criminal charges, specifically insult laws, to silence journalists and adversaries. The newspaper highlights a confusion between calumny, injury, and defamation, suggesting these distinctions are being blurred to enable prosecutions.

The publication points to Article 213 of the Penal Code concerning insult, defining it as an attack on a person's intimacy. Examples provided include accusations spread on social media about a former partner's physical attributes and derogatory remarks made in public debates or school settings.

Folha 8 argues that these legal actions, even when based on suspicion, are used to target individuals and suppress their ability to express themselves freely. The newspaper indicates this practice is becoming a rule rather than an exception in the country.

bj.headline: Benin's Supreme Court opens judicial year
bj.dek: Vice President Mariam Chabi Talata officially launched the new judicial year on November 5, 2026.
paragraphs: The President of the Economic and Social Council (CES), Abdoulaye Bio Tchané, attended the solemn opening of the Supreme Court's judicial year on Thursday, November 5, 2026, in Porto-Novo. The event, themed "The Electoral Judge and the Stakes of Local Democracy," highlighted justice's role in upholding the rule of law and managing elections. Vice President Mariam Chabi Talata, representing the Head of State, officially opened the new judicial year.

Supreme Court President Victor Dassi Adoussou presided over the ceremony, acknowledging the presence of institutional leaders, including Bio Tchané. Bio Tchané's attendance demonstrated the CES's commitment to inter-institutional synergy, emphasizing dialogue and cooperation for national development. This participation signals the CES's dedication to strengthening democratic institutions.

The Supreme Court's new judicial year, 2026-2027, focuses on the electoral judge's role in local democracy. The ceremony underscored the importance of justice in maintaining democratic balance and the rule of law. The CES reaffirmed its commitment to inter-institutional collaboration for Benin's progress.

bj.headline: Benin book celebrates 41 inspiring figures
bj.dek: The "Those Who Inspire Benin" collection aims to guide young people through the experiences of successful individuals.
paragraphs: The Novotel in Cotonou hosted the launch of "Those Who Inspire Benin" on Wednesday, November 4, 2026. The book features 41 portraits of Beninese women and men recognized for their professional and civic achievements. Canal+ sponsored the event, which brought together institutional figures, business leaders, and young people.

Marlène Plomik, founder of the international "Those Who Inspire" movement, stated that this 17th edition, focused on Benin, aims to provide concrete guidance for students and young professionals. The book will be distributed for free in public universities, accompanied by direct exchanges between featured individuals and students during "Inspiring Days."

Local project coordinator Izar Hyacinthe explained that the book's creation involved a full year of research, interviews, and writing. Several individuals featured in the book, including scientist Moumouni Adamou, entrepreneur Lionel Talon, and public health specialist Ghislaine Loko Djidjoho, shared their career paths and societal contributions during the launch event.

bj.headline: Benin president replaces military high command
bj.dek: General Abou Issa, who survived a coup attempt, now leads the military after a complete reshuffle on November 4.
paragraphs: Benin's entire military high command was replaced on November 4, with General Abou Issa appointed to lead the new structure. Issa is an experienced officer who previously survived an attempted coup on December 7, 2025. The reshuffle was approved by the Council of Ministers and announced by the Minister of Defence.

Speculation about a military reorganization had circulated for months within the Benin army. President Romuald Wadagni, who was inaugurated on May 24, has now acted on these rumors. The previous high command was removed following this decision.

The announcement was made on November 4, with a modification to the report published the following day. The military changes come after the celebration of Benin's 66th anniversary of national and international sovereignty on August 1, 2026.

bw.headline: Botswana nominates Gevorg Tamamyan for WHO top job

paragraphs: President Duma Boko has formally proposed Dr. Gevorg Tamamyan for the World Health Organization's Director-General position, with the nomination letter sent to the WHO Executive Board chairperson. The World Health Assembly will consider the appointment in May 2027.

Boko explained Botswana's decision by stating that the country's health-system challenges highlight the need for effective global health leadership. He met Tamamyan and was satisfied with his commitment to underserved communities, leading Botswana to put his name forward.

Tamamyan is one of seven candidates announced by the WHO on October 29. A candidates' forum is scheduled for November 18–19 in Geneva, and the Executive Board will narrow the field to five in early 2027, with the new Director-General taking office on August 16, 2027.

bw.headline: Botswana Vaccine Institute faces export threat
bw.dek: Namibia and South Africa plan domestic vaccine production, potentially reducing demand for Botswana's foot-and-mouth disease exports.
paragraphs: Botswana Vaccine Institute (BVI) faces a potential long-term threat to its export business as Namibia and South Africa develop their own foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) vaccine manufacturing capabilities. Namibia plans to establish its own plant, aiming to reduce reliance on imported vaccines, despite a recent three-year deal for over 3.8 million doses from Botswana valued at P50.43 million.

Ben Haraseb, Namibia's director for agricultural production, outlined the plant plans in October at an expo in Windhoek. While Botswana is Namibia's current main supplier, the immediate risk to BVI is limited due to the existing supply agreement and the fact that Namibia's facility is not yet operational. However, successful local production could eventually decrease Namibian orders.

South Africa also resumed domestic FMD vaccine production in February 2026 through the Agricultural Research Council (ARC), after a two-decade hiatus. The ARC handed over its first locally produced batch on February 6. These developments in key export markets raise concerns for BVI's future regional sales.

bw.headline: Batswana approval of China's influence halves in a decade
bw.dek: Afrobarometer survey shows favourable views dropping from 74% to 37% between 2014 and 2024.
paragraphs: Batswana's positive views on China's influence have fallen by half over the past decade, according to a new Afrobarometer survey.

The proportion of citizens seeing China's influence as positive dropped from 74 percent in 2014 to 37 percent in 2024, a decrease of 37 percentage points. Only 50 percent of Batswana now believe China's economic activities significantly influence the national economy, down from 76 percent in 2014.
Men and urban residents are more likely than women and rural dwellers to view China's influence as substantial and beneficial.

bw.headline: Botswana women's football faces funding gap
bw.dek: A new 20-team league launched this year requires more sponsorship to sustain its growth and player development.
paragraphs: Women's football in Botswana is expanding with the introduction of a 20-team National First Division, split into northern and southern conferences. However, the Botswana Football Association (BFA) warns that a lack of sponsorship and suitable infrastructure threatens the league's progress. Clubs need financial backing for transport, equipment, coaching, and facilities to support the increased opportunities for players.

Tsholofelo Setlhoko, BFA Head of Women’s Football, stated that while the new league represents significant growth, clubs are struggling with funding shortages. She met with representatives from the African Club Association (ACA), an independent body aiming to support clubs across the continent, to explore potential partnerships. Setlhoko, also a FIFA Women’s Football Development Expert, highlighted the need for dependable backing to meet weekly operational costs.

The BFA is seeking ways to build on the momentum of the new division, aiming to provide a more secure foundation for players and clubs. Regional competitions, like the existing women's club tournament, offer chances for teams to improve skills and raise their playing standards by competing against diverse styles. BFA president Tariq Babitseng is also discussing a regional men's club tournament.

bw.headline: 4,274 foreigners gained Botswana citizenship via marriage
bw.dek: Zimbabweans and South Africans married to Batswana citizens acquired citizenship between 2018 and 2026.
paragraphs: Government figures show that 4,274 Zimbabwean and South African nationals became Botswana citizens through marriage between 2018 and 2026. Of this total, 2,947 were Zimbabweans and 1,327 were South Africans, with Zimbabweans making up about 69 percent of the beneficiaries.

Minister of Labour and Home Affairs Pius Mokgware stated that geographical proximity and shared borders facilitate relationships leading to these marriages. He explained that cross-border movement has contributed to relationships where foreign spouses seek Botswana citizenship. Marriage to a Motswana does not automatically grant citizenship; applicants must meet naturalisation requirements.

The Citizenship Act requires foreign spouses to have resided in Botswana for at least five years and lodged a declaration of intention to apply for naturalisation two and a half years before their application. Minister Mokgware disclosed these figures in response to a question in Ntlo ya Dikgosi.

Authorities and craft sector representatives from the three Alliance des États du Sahel (AES) countries reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening economic, cultural, and professional exchanges.

Alassane Ouédraogo, secretary general of Burkina Faso's Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Artisans, welcomed the Malian and Nigerien delegations, noting their participation gave the SIAO edition a special dimension.

Ouédraogo stated that Burkina Faso, Mali, and Niger are linked by common history, traditions, and aspirations for development, with this fraternity now finding new momentum through the AES confederation. He urged concrete adoption of this vision by populations and economic actors, particularly through trade and private sector initiatives.

bf.headline: Burkina Faso not informed of Guinean artisanal mining expulsions
bf.dek: Thousands of Burkinabe artisanal miners were forced to leave Guinea's Siguiri region.
paragraphs: Thousands of young Burkinabe artisanal miners were forced to leave Guinea's Siguiri administrative region. Guinean authorities cited environmental reasons and illegal activity for suspending artisanal mining operations and expelling workers. Burkinabe Minister of Security Mahamadou Sana stated that Burkina Faso was not officially informed of the operation.

Guinean officials claim artisanal mining pollutes land and water and threatens local populations. However, the Burkinabe government believes a lack of official consultation between the two nations contributed to the crisis. This situation has sparked debate on social media, with differing views on artisanal mining.

The expulsion of Burkinabe citizens from Guinea highlights a lack of diplomatic tact, according to the report. A high-level meeting or official communication between the two countries could have provided a more humane resolution to the crisis.

bf.headline: Burkina Faso school councils meet on education reforms
bf.dek: Bané school leaders gathered on November 4, 2026, to discuss their role in implementing educational changes.
paragraphs: School council presidents and headteachers in Bané, Burkina Faso, met on Tuesday, November 4, 2026, to discuss their role in implementing educational reforms. The meeting, led by the head of the Basic Education Circumscription (CEB) Théodore ZOUGMORE, took place at Bané Mixed School. ZOUGMORE credited the school councils' support for the 97% success rate in the 2025-2026 primary school certificate exams.

Primary education supervisor Bangré Locré urged council members to create action plans for their schools by November 15, 2026, and to manage finances transparently. He also called for their involvement in preventing and managing risks from terrorist incursions by sharing information. The reforms discussed included vocational training, civic education, bilingual teaching, and the responsible use of digital technologies.

The reforms aim to reveal students' aptitudes for future employment through practical activities like school gardens and livestock. Civic education will focus on respect for laws and national values, including wearing helmets and respecting national symbols. Bilingual education, using national languages, is intended to improve learning and preserve linguistic heritage, with councils encouraged to promote traditional attire.

bi.headline: Burundi engineer disappears from sugar company
bi.dek: Three SOSUMO managers questioned by prosecutors after the agricultural equipment maintenance chief went missing on October 30.
paragraphs: Ismaël Mugisha, deputy head of agricultural equipment maintenance at the Moso Sugar Company (SOSUMO) in Rutana province, has been missing since October 30. Three SOSUMO managers, Arnaud Nikuze, Jean Claude Ntwari, and Aimé Clovis Irakoze, were questioned by the Makamba Court of Appeal prosecutor on November 3 regarding his disappearance. Mugisha, who had worked at SOSUMO for four years, was last seen leaving his home for work on the morning of October 30.

Colleagues reported seeing Mugisha at his office that morning, while others did not see him, leaving his exact movements unclear. Internal sources suggest disagreements over the maintenance and management of agricultural equipment, with Mugisha reportedly advocating for repairs over new purchases. Some colleagues expressed suspicions of mismanagement and potential embezzlement related to equipment procurement and upkeep, though these claims are unproven. Mugisha had also told colleagues he felt threatened by some individuals.

SOSUMO announced Mugisha's disappearance in local churches on November 1. The company has been investigating the circumstances surrounding his vanishing, with the prosecutor's office now involved in the inquiry. The investigation aims to clarify the events leading up to his disappearance and determine if any foul play was involved.

cm.headline: Douala industries may get 170 MW more power by year-end
cm.dek: World Bank official announced the potential power boost for Cameroon's economic capital after meeting the finance minister.
paragraphs: Industries in Douala, Cameroon's economic capital, may gain access to an additional 170 MW of electricity by the end of 2026. Cheick Fantamady Kanté, the World Bank's division director for Cameroon and four other Central African countries, announced this outlook on October 30 in Yaoundé. This additional supply is for businesses and does not increase the Nachtigal hydropower plant's 420 MW generation capacity from its seven operational units.

The potential for 170 MW more electricity for Douala industries by year-end follows months of delays in building a second transmission corridor. Progress on this infrastructure is key to delivering more power from the Nachtigal plant to the Littoral region. Water and Energy Minister Gaston Eloundou Essomba inspected the site on October 7, 2026, and set November as a deadline for transmission infrastructure progress.
The availability of this extra power by year-end depends on progress with the transmission infrastructure. Kanté's announcement came after a meeting with Finance Minister Louis Paul Motaze.

cm.headline: Cameroon secures CFA174.6 billion for Dibamba bridge
cm.dek: French Development Agency, EIB, and EU provide funding for road and bridge reconstruction.
paragraphs: Cameroon has secured CFA174.6 billion in financing for the reconstruction of the Edéa-Douala road and the construction of a second bridge over the Dibamba River. The funding package was presented to Public Works Minister Emmanuel Nganou Djoumessi on November 2, 2026, by a delegation from the French Development Agency (AFD), the European Investment Bank (EIB), and the European Union. This financing covers the road reconstruction, the new bridge, and the rehabilitation of the existing bridge.

The total proposed financing includes €125 million from AFD, €100 million from the EIB, and €39.2 million from the European Union. While the project aims to improve infrastructure, the role of Canadian contractor Magil Construction remains unclear. Magil had signed a contract in December 2019 for a project that included a second bridge, but budget issues later limited financing to road works. Magil submitted a new financing proposal for the bridge in February 2026, but the government has not confirmed if it is still being considered.

The funding package totals €264.2 million, with the remaining amount to be covered. The reconstruction of the Edéa-Douala section of National Highway N3 is a key component of the project. The government has not yet clarified Magil Construction's involvement in the bridge construction despite their previous contract and a recent financing proposal.

cm.headline: PlaYce Cameroun raises capital by CFA2.19 billion
cm.dek: The shopping mall operator increased its share capital by 14.5% to CFA17.285 billion after issuing new shares.
paragraphs: PlaYce Cameroun has increased its share capital by CFA2.19 billion, raising it from CFA15.095 billion to CFA17.285 billion. The company's board confirmed the transaction on September 28, 2026, following approval at a June 30 meeting. This capital increase represents 14.5% of the company's previous share capital and involved issuing 219,007 new shares at CFA10,000 each, all paid for in cash.

The legal notice, prepared by notary Gisèle Enguélé Dipanda, states that the shares were fully paid in cash. Article 7 of the company's bylaws concerning share capital was amended, and documents were filed with the Douala-Bonanjo Court of First Instance. The notice does not identify who subscribed to the new shares or the post-transaction ownership structure.

As of March 31, 2026, French holding company PlaYce SAS, part of the CFAO group, owned 99.99% of PlaYce Cameroun, according to its annual financial statements. This ownership figure predates the recent capital increase.

cm.headline: Cameroon police arrest fake presidential security agent
cm.dek: Authorities seized firearms, military uniforms, and fake presidential passes from two individuals in Yaoundé.
paragraphs: National gendarmerie in Yaoundé arrested two men in separate operations, seizing two firearms. Colonel Désiré Joseph Nguele, commander of the Centre Gendarmerie Legion, coordinated the arrests.

In Ebom, a 39-year-old man was arrested for posing as a Directorate of Presidential Security (DSP) agent to scam people with false recruitment promises. Investigators found a pistol, military uniforms, and fake presidential passes at his home.

A second suspect was apprehended in the Carrière neighborhood with a German-made revolver and six cartridges. He admitted to past robberies in the Moungo department. Both men are in custody as investigations continue.

cf.headline: Bangui floods leave over 2,000 homeless
cf.dek: The Ministry of Humanitarian Action is distributing essential kits to those affected by recent heavy rains.
paragraphs: Heavy rains in Bangui and its outskirts have left over 2,000 people homeless. The Ministry of Humanitarian Action, with support from the UNHCR, is distributing essential kits to affected residents in the 4th arrondissement. These kits include items like tarpaulins, buckets, mats, and cooking pots.

Minister of Humanitarian Action, Lina Josiane Bemakassoui, stated on Monday in Bangui that efforts are underway to assist the victims, despite facing difficulties. Residents from sectors 4 I and 4 II gathered at the 4th arrondissement police station to receive aid. Wini Edoxie Yakona, a resident, described losing all her belongings when the Ngouya Bagara canal overflowed into her home.

The head of Dedengué 4 neighborhood, Dieudonné Ngofio, urged the government to build more canals to improve water flow and reduce future flood risks. He also noted that some flooding is caused by residents dumping waste into drainage channels. The Ministry has called on partners to provide further assistance to the affected population.

cf.headline: Central African Republic fuel prices rise, transport costs follow
cf.dek: Transport fares increase in Bangui one month after fuel prices went up at the pump.
paragraphs: Fuel prices have risen in Bangui, the capital of the Central African Republic, one month after the initial increase at the pump. This situation is linked to both the higher cost of fuel and its scarcity. Prices for transport, particularly for vehicles running on gasoline, are now negotiated individually.

Trade unionist Nicaise Ngouandji described the government's communication on the fuel price hike as a "return of the head tax that does not say its name." He criticized the decision as anti-social and imposed without consultation, making Central Africans the "financial and technical partner" of a struggling state.
The increase in transport costs affects the daily lives of citizens in Bangui. The government has not announced specific next steps regarding fuel availability or pricing adjustments.

cf.headline: Central African Republic governance score drops
cf.dek: The country ranks 50th out of 54 African nations in the 2026 Mo Ibrahim Foundation governance report.
paragraphs: The Central African Republic's governance has significantly declined, scoring only 31.3 out of 100 according to the 2026 Mo Ibrahim Foundation report. The country now ranks 50th among 54 African states, losing 0.9 points over the past decade.

This assessment covers most of President Faustin Archange Touadéra's tenure since 2016. While some economic and social progress was noted, it was outweighed by a deterioration in public freedoms, political participation, and institutional effectiveness.
The report, focusing on the 2016-2025 period, highlights that improvements in certain areas did not compensate for the decline in governance indicators.

cf.headline: Four killed near Tiringoulou
cf.dek: Unidentified armed men killed four young men returning from a gold mine.
paragraphs: Four people were killed last Monday about 30 kilometers from Tiringoulou, on the Birao axis in the Vakaga region. The victims, young men returning from a gold mine, were killed by unidentified armed men. The mayor of Ouandja commune, Al-Abib Yaya, spoke about the circumstances of the killings.

Russian mercenaries from the Wagner group killed four young Central Africans of the Kara ethnic group between Tiringoulou and Délémbé. The bodies were decapitated and then burned with their motorcycles. One of the victims was identified as a member of the self-defense militia known as the Black Wagner.
The incident occurred near the village of Délémbé.

km.headline: Omani delegation meets Comorian police chiefs
km.dek: Officials from Oman's interior ministry visited Moroni to discuss security cooperation and capacity building.
paragraphs: A three-person delegation from Oman's Ministry of Interior arrived in Comoros on November 4 and met with national police authorities on November 5 to discuss security cooperation. The delegation, led by General Jamal Habib Abdullah Al Quraishi, director general of Judicial Police, met with Comoros' Minister of Interior Mohamed Ahmed Assoumani.

During a working session, Comorian police officials, including Controller General Nassif Kaissane and his deputy, Commissioner Mohamed Achikali Yahaya, discussed strengthening institutional capacities with the Omani visitors. The delegation also visited the central police station in Moroni and the Judicial Police premises at Dar Sanda to observe operational structures.

The mission aims to consolidate relations and explore new collaborations between Comoros and Oman. The specific commitments and their implementation timeline were not detailed in the police national communiqué.

cg.headline: Congo's energy loop project to expand to new countries
cg.dek: The Central Africa Energy Pool wants to connect more countries to a regional electricity grid.
paragraphs: The Central Africa Energy Pool (PEAC) plans to expand its energy loop project to include more countries in the sub-region. This initiative aims to boost electricity exchanges and strengthen grid interconnections across Central Africa. The project, initially planned for the Republic of Congo, Angola, and the Democratic Republic of Congo, could now incorporate additional states.

Discussions on November 5 in Brazzaville between Congo's Energy Minister Bruno Jean Richard Itoua and PEAC leadership, including Director Committee President Rui Pereira Do Amaral Gourgel, focused on this expansion. The PEAC seeks to accelerate regional energy integration amid ongoing challenges with electricity access and supply security in several nations.

The project also involves the potential construction of the 600 MW Chollet hydroelectric dam. The PEAC's goal is to promote better sharing of energy resources and speed up the development of common infrastructure, using grid interconnections as a tool for energy security and economic growth in Central Africa.

cg.headline: Brazzaville court opens criminal session with murder cases
cg.dek: The Court of Appeal in Brazzaville will hear dozens of criminal cases including murder and state security charges over three months.
paragraphs: The Court of Appeal in Brazzaville opened its criminal session on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, with proceedings set to run through January 2027. 10 jurors were sworn in to assist professional magistrates. The session will examine approximately 50 criminal cases, including the assassination of Anne Félicité Massamba-Débat, daughter of a former president, who was killed on June 13, 2023.

Five individuals are accused in the Massamba-Débat murder case. The court will also hear the case of lawyer Bob Kaben Massouka, detained since July 2025, who faces charges of criminal conspiracy and attempting to undermine state security with six co-accused. Another case involves about 20 people, mostly foreigners, charged with criminal conspiracy, passport forgery, and corruption.

The first day's hearings focused on aggravated theft and murder charges against several individuals, including a fugitive known as "Maréchal Mbibo." The session aims to address serious offenses against personal integrity over the next three months.

cg.headline: Congo launches third phase of health security program
cg.dek: Prime Minister Anatole Collinet Makosso presided over the launch of the HeSP program's third phase in Brazzaville.
paragraphs: Republic of Congo Prime Minister Anatole Collinet Makosso officially launched the third phase of the West and Central Africa Health Security Program (HeSP) in Brazzaville on Tuesday, November 3, 2026. The launch occurred during a regional conference focused on strengthening health security, which gathered nearly 180 participants from various states, regional institutions, and international partners.

The third phase of the program involves the Congo, Cameroon, the Central African Republic, and Chad. Its aim is to improve epidemiological surveillance and enhance national capacities for preventing and responding to health emergencies. The initiative seeks to better anticipate health risks and coordinate interventions against epidemics that could cross borders.

The regional meeting provides a platform for exchanging experiences and best practices in preventing and managing health threats. The participating states intend to consolidate cooperation mechanisms and develop more effective early warning systems to address shared health challenges.

cg.headline: Congo plans stronger epidemic response
cg.dek: Brazzaville conference concludes with calls to boost surveillance and research for regional health security.
paragraphs: Republic of Congo's regional integration minister, Ludovic Ngatsé, announced on November 4 in Brazzaville that a recent conference will help the sub-region enhance its capacity to fight epidemics. The meeting's conclusions urge strengthening surveillance systems, consolidating the "One Health" approach, developing human resources, and promoting research and innovation to build a regional health security community.

Health professionals from Central and West Africa shared experiences over two days, formulating recommendations to prevent and manage health crises. These include sustainable financing, maintaining calm during crises, applying the "One Health" approach, and prioritizing prevention, as crisis management is more costly than prevention. CEMAC vice-president Assamba Angondo stated that health security is essential for stability and prosperity, as a country's epidemic prevention capacity contributes to its neighbors' security.

Minister Ngatsé praised the conference's exchanges and reaffirmed Congo's commitment to supporting this collective ambition and strengthening health response nationally and regionally. The conference highlighted that cooperation is a necessity for regional health security.

cg.headline: Fondation Mérieux urges unified viral threat approach
cg.dek: Alain Mérieux met with Congo's science minister to discuss a global 'One Health' strategy against epidemics.
paragraphs: Alain Mérieux, president of Fondation Mérieux, stated on November 3 in Brazzaville that a unified approach is needed to combat viral threats. He emphasized that African countries must open borders to face viruses that do not respect them, advocating for an interconnected and global response involving countries, doctors, veterinarians, and environmental specialists.

Mérieux explained that the response to epidemics can no longer be isolated, promoting the 'One Health' concept championed by Professor Ntoumi. Fondation Mérieux, active in 15 countries facing security or health crises, intends to serve Congo's needs, acknowledging the globalization of infection risks and the need for joint responses from foundations, laboratories like Institut Pasteur, and various nations, citing Ebola and monkeypox as lessons.

The Fondation Mérieux president assured that the Congolese government is open to collaboration and praised local expertise, particularly Professor Francine Ntoumi, for her ability to train scientists. He expressed confidence in Congo's scientific community, which is forming a school of doctors and biologists to meet these needs, concluding that a seven-year collaboration has been tacitly renewed.

ci.headline: PETROCI ships first crude oil cargo as operator
ci.dek: The national oil company's subsidiary loaded its first shipment from the Espoir field on October 31, 2026.
paragraphs: The Ivorian national oil company, PETROCI, shipped its first crude oil cargo on October 31, 2026, three months after taking over operations of the Espoir field. This marks PETROCI CI-26, a subsidiary fully owned by PETROCI Holding, becoming the direct operator of the offshore field near Jacqueville. This operation signifies the state-owned company's transition from a partner to a direct operator in oil asset exploitation.

This first lifting, or crude oil loading for transport, confirms the operational implementation of PETROCI's new role. Previously, PETROCI Holding primarily held stakes in projects managed by international groups, such as the Baleine field operated by Eni. Now, PETROCI directly manages the Espoir field's production, offshore maintenance, and crude oil loading, a responsibility previously held by Canadian Natural Resources (CNR).

The Espoir field, discovered in 1980 and redeveloped for production in February 2002, is now under the direct management of PETROCI CI-26, led by Mabintou Tatiana Cissé. The next steps for PETROCI involve sustaining production, controlling costs, and building national capacity in oil exploitation. The volume of this initial cargo, the buyer, and its destination were not publicly disclosed.

ci.headline: Amad Diallo nominated for African Player of the Year
ci.dek: The Manchester United winger is the sole Ivorian contender for the 2026 award, to be presented in Lagos.
paragraphs: The Confederation of African Football (CAF) announced its 10 nominees for the 2026 African Player of the Year award on Wednesday, November 4. Amad Diallo of Manchester United is the only Ivorian player on the list, competing against three nominees each from Morocco and Senegal. The winner will be revealed on December 7 in Lagos, Nigeria.

Diallo represents Ivory Coast alone among the 10 selected players, who hail from six different nations. Morocco's Achraf Hakimi, the 2025 titleholder, is nominated alongside Brahim Díaz and Ismaël Saibari. Senegal's contenders are Sadio Mané, Ismaïla Sarr, and Pape Gueye. Other nominees include Yoane Wissa (DR Congo), Antoine Semenyo (Ghana), and Teboho Mokoena (South Africa).

Hakimi is considered a strong contender due to his status as the reigning champion and Morocco's multiple nominations. Diallo faces the challenge of overcoming a difficult season with Manchester United. The CAF Awards ceremony will also announce winners in other categories, such as best goalkeeper, where Morocco's Yassine Bounou is nominated.

eg.headline: Egyptian-American Abdul El-Sayed wins Michigan Senate seat
eg.dek: El-Sayed becomes the first Muslim to serve in the US Senate after a close race against Republican Mike Rogers.
paragraphs: Egyptian-American Abdul El-Sayed won a Michigan Senate seat on Wednesday, November 4, defeating Republican Mike Rogers. El-Sayed, 42, a former public health administrator, is the first Muslim elected to the United States Senate.

The campaign against El-Sayed involved heavy outside spending and attacks, including claims of communism and baseless ties to terrorism. El-Sayed thanked supporters for taking a chance on "the unlikeliest of candidates" after a campaign he described as among the ugliest. The seat was previously held by retiring Democrat Senator Gary Peters.

Egyptian billionaire Naguib Sawiris defended El-Sayed on X, calling him "resilient, sharp, and charismatic" and dismissing accusations of Muslim Brotherhood ties. Sawiris stated that El-Sayed earned his victory on merit, following a viral town hall exchange where El-Sayed disavowed any connection to the group.

eg.headline: Egypt and IFAD sign $65M irrigation deals
eg.dek: Agreements aim to modernize water management across 12,600 hectares and train 2,000 people.
paragraphs: Egypt has signed two agricultural financing agreements totalling US$65.32 million with the International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD) to modernize irrigation and boost climate resilience. The majority of the funds, US$64.85 million, will support the CROWN project, aiming to improve water efficiency and farmer incomes across 12,600 hectares.

The CROWN project is expected to benefit approximately 90,000 rural households by modernizing irrigation and drainage systems and promoting climate-smart farming practices. A separate US$470,000 grant for the PEARL project will enhance agricultural expertise in Egyptian institutions through training and digital tools for about 2,000 individuals.

Egypt faces water scarcity with less than 500 cubic meters per person annually, prompting a focus on efficiency rather than supply. The Nile provides over 98% of the country's water resources, making modernization crucial amid population growth and increasing food demand.

eg.headline: Egypt court hears Giza Pyramids rave ban case
eg.dek: A lawsuit filed by the Egyptian Center for Economic and Social Rights seeks to stop loud music and light shows at the ancient site.
paragraphs: Egypt's State Council Administrative Court has postponed a case seeking to ban rave parties and laser light shows at the Giza Pyramids until January 2, 2027. The Egyptian Center for Economic and Social Rights (ECESR) filed the lawsuit against the Minister of Tourism and Antiquities and other officials. The case challenges the state's alleged inaction regarding commercial entertainment within the Giza Pyramids perimeter.

Lawyers for ECESR argued that loud, low-frequency sound systems pose structural risks to the ancient masonry, and high-powered laser displays violate UNESCO guidelines for World Heritage sites. The suit also demands a halt to temporary earthworks and staging installations within the monument's buffer zone. Prominent preservationists, including Egyptologist Monica Hanna, are supporting the action.

The litigation is grounded in Egypt's Constitution, Antiquities Law #117/1983, and international UNESCO treaties. The ECESR is petitioning for an immediate halt to all event licensing and a full audit of current commercial vendor contracts operating at the Giza Pyramids.

eg.dek: The Egyptian athlete secured the nation's first Youth Olympic medal in wushu with a combined score of 18.660 points.
paragraphs: Egyptian wushu athlete Sondos Sonbol won gold in the women’s Changquan combined event at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games on Tuesday, 3 November. This victory marks Egypt's first Youth Olympic medal in the martial art, which debuted as an official sport in Dakar.

Sonbol achieved a combined score of 18.660 points, surpassing Venezuela's Valeria Frannerys Dudamel Alvarado (18.199) and India's Rajkumari Lanchenbi Chanu (18.039). She led both wushu disciplines, scoring 9.330 points in the staff-based Gunshu and maintaining her lead in Changquan.

Wushu combines traditional combat with choreographed athletic movements, including kicks, jumps, and routines, with some disciplines using weapons. Sonbol's win is a significant achievement for the sport's debut at the Youth Olympic Games.

eg.headline: Egypt to play role in AI governance
eg.dek: Academics and diplomats met at New Giza University to discuss Egypt's potential influence in AI development and global economic shifts.
paragraphs: New Giza University, with the University of Glasgow, hosted a conference on artificial intelligence's growing role in national power and global economics. The event explored how AI is reshaping international influence, with discussions highlighting Egypt's potential to lead in the new order due to its geography and strategic weight.

Participants discussed Egypt's opportunities to increase its involvement in global trade, investment, and production chains, and to help set rules for cybersecurity and artificial intelligence. The forum also addressed the risks of wealth concentrating in a few hands and the necessity for states to regulate markets for equitable benefit distribution.

The conference celebrated New Giza University's 10th anniversary and the 250th anniversary of Adam Smith's "The Wealth of Nations." Speakers cautioned that technology could become a tool for conflict among major global powers.

gq.headline: Equatorial Guinea court sentences 13 to prison
gq.dek: Judgments include 13 years for homicide, nine years for fraud, and five years for rape.
paragraphs: The Provincial Court of Litoral in Equatorial Guinea has issued sentences in recent criminal trials. Josué Mba Micha received 13 years in prison for homicide, and José Ramón Nvo Mangue was sentenced to 10 years for the same crime. Rodrigo Félix was given nine years for three fraud offenses and ordered to repay over two million CFA francs to victims.

Tikou Divian Tiku faces seven years and eight months for robbery and another seven years and eight months for serious injury. Fidel Ndong Nguema Abuy was sentenced to five years and three months for raping a 13-year-old girl, along with a fine of 2,525,000 CFA francs. Joaquín Ovono Nkuna received a five-year prison term.

Bonifacio Pedro Esono Ondo will serve three years and four months and pay a 2,525,000 CFA franc fine, while Bernardo Obiang Nkua got three years of major arrest. Other sentences include six months for Benito Alogo Nvele for injuries, one year for Juan Carlos Oyono for drug offenses, and two years for Virginia Mikue for serious injuries. Ramón Owono Obiang received three years for fraud. The court also issued acquittals in several cases, including one for alleged HIV transmission.

gq.headline: Confucius Institute marks 10 years in Malabo
gq.dek: The UNGE institute has trained 2,636 students, with 97.76% being Equatoguinean nationals.
paragraphs: The Confucius Institute at the National University of Equatorial Guinea (UNGE) celebrated its tenth anniversary on Wednesday at the UNGE central campus in Malabo. The event featured an academic and cultural atmosphere, highlighting the institute's established presence in the country. The institute received a donation of books from China's Zhejiang University.

Director Fernando Panadez García reported that 2,636 students have passed through the institute over the decade, with 97.76% being Equatoguinean. The student body also includes individuals from Cuba, Spain, Cameroon, Nigeria, Madagascar, Gabon, Guinea, Brazil, China, Lebanon, Mali, and Russia. Women constitute the majority of students, with 1,456 enrolled compared to 1,180 men.

The institute aims to foster connections between Chinese and Equatoguinean cultures through language and academic exchange. Chinese Ambassador Wang Wengang acknowledged the institute's role in strengthening institutional development and pedagogical models. The UNGE Confucius Institute operates under the joint guidance of UNGE and Zhejiang University of Foreign Languages.

er.headline: US lifts sanctions on Eritrea
er.dek: Sanctions removed on September 19, 2026, targeted the ruling party's financial and military apparatus.
paragraphs: The United States removed sanctions on Eritrea on September 19, 2026. These sanctions were imposed in 2021 due to Eritrea’s involvement in the Tigray War. The US government had outlined plans to lift the sanctions four months prior, according to a Reuters report.

Human rights groups criticized the decision, citing Eritrea's record of forced labor and torture under the ruling People’s Front for Democracy and Justice (PFDJ). Eritrea's government called the sanctions 'illicit and immoral' and claimed they caused 'incalculable damage' and constrained development.

The removed sanctions targeted the PFDJ’s financial and military bodies and two officials, Abraha Kassa and Hagos Gebrehiwet. The Eritrean Defence Force’s chief of staff, Filipos Woldeyohannes, remains under separate sanctions. The PFDJ has previously benefited from the removal of UN sanctions in 2018, remaining self-sufficient.

ke.headline: Former LSK president demands prosecution for Migori attack
ke.dek: Opposition leaders Kalonzo Musyoka, Eugene Wamalwa and Justin Muturi were attacked on November 5, 2026, in Migori.
paragraphs: Former Law Society of Kenya President Faith Odhiambo demanded the prosecution of attackers who disrupted an opposition tour in Migori on Thursday, November 5, 2026. The attack targeted opposition leaders Kalonzo Musyoka, Eugene Wamalwa, and Justin Muturi, damaging several vehicles in their convoy. Odhiambo stated that the incident violated the leaders' constitutional rights to political participation and freedom of expression.

Odhiambo expressed concern over recurring political violence and insufficient action by authorities, noting that shattered windows can be replaced but a life lost cannot. She called for police to identify and investigate those who organised or financed the violence, and for an independent inquiry into police conduct during the confrontation. The leaders were in the South Nyanza region for political mobilisation ahead of the 2027 General Election.

The convoy was pelted with stones by approximately 10 youths, causing damage to vehicles including Muturi's and Musyoka's cars. Running battles between suspected attackers and police, who used teargas, followed the incident. Despite the disruption, the opposition leaders vowed to continue their political engagements.

ke.headline: UN-Habitat, IGAD launch El Niño flood guide for Horn of Africa cities
ke.dek: The new framework helps city leaders prepare for heavy rainfall and protect vulnerable communities before disasters strike.
paragraphs: UN-Habitat and the Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD) launched a preparedness framework on November 6 to help cities in the Greater Horn of Africa prepare for El Niño flooding. The guide, developed with ICPAC, aims to shift city authorities from disaster response to proactive preparation using climate forecasts.

The advisory, titled El Niño Preparedness: An Anticipatory Action Framework for City Leaders, offers practical steps for municipal governments to mobilize resources, strengthen warning systems, and protect infrastructure. It addresses heightened risks in informal settlements and flood-prone neighborhoods amid expectations of heavy rainfall.

The framework outlines how city leaders can translate forecasts into concrete decisions by using impact-based scenarios, pre-agreed action triggers, anticipatory financing, and stronger coordination. It also identifies sector-specific measures to reduce the effects of flooding and disease outbreaks on urban populations.

ke.headline: Kenya targets sugar export market in three years
ke.dek: The Bura Irrigation Scheme aims to boost sugarcane production with yields double those of other regions.
paragraphs: Kenya aims to enter the international sugar export market within three years through a public-private partnership at the Bura Irrigation Scheme in Tana River County. The government has leased 135,000 acres of the 176,000-acre scheme to investors, including Sukari Industries and Tana River Sugar, who will cultivate sugarcane on 50,000 acres each. This expansion is supported by a new 26-kilometre gravity canal delivering water from the Tana River.

Head of Public Service Felix Koskei stated that the coastal region was chosen for its land and water resources, noting sugarcane matures in 10 months there, faster than in Western Kenya or Nyanza. Irrigation Principal Secretary Ephantus Kimotho added that the scheme could achieve 50 tonnes per hectare, double the yield elsewhere, with the 100,000 acres for sugarcane expected to produce over five million metric tonnes per harvest.

This project is part of efforts to increase sugarcane production and strengthen Kenya's regional sugar market position, reversing a 24.5% drop in domestic production in 2025. The government anticipates meeting domestic demand and creating a surplus for export within four years.

ke.headline: Kenyan pathologists find over 20 wounds on murdered 86-year-old
ke.dek: Three doctors examined Dorita Lasinder Macharia after her death on October 30, 2026, at her Loresho home.
paragraphs: Pathologists found more than 20 injuries on Dorita Lasinder Macharia, 86, who died on the night of October 30, 2026, at her Loresho home. Three doctors conducted a post-mortem examination at Lee Funeral Home, revealing multiple stab wounds to the neck that caused severe bleeding. The examination also noted a fracture on her left upper arm and other sharp-force injuries across her body. Investigators are working to determine the exact weapon used and are examining collected samples.

The post-mortem findings were revealed on Tuesday, November 2, as five people, including the deceased's daughter Regina Wambui Gitao, alias Regina Re, were arrested. Detectives from Gigiri sought 15 days to detain the suspects for further investigation, but the court granted them 10 days. Police Constable David Njoroge stated that preliminary findings suggest a disagreement between Dorita and her granddaughter, Thandie Malaika Wanjiku Gitao, over Thandie's boyfriend, Alton Jimmy Macharia, preceded the incident.

The investigator told the court that Dorita had asked Thandie to leave the house after finding her in a compromising situation with Alton. Dorita then called her son, Jimmy, to assist in evicting her granddaughter. Although Thandie reportedly left, she later returned and stayed with Dorita for about an hour before the elderly woman was found dead. Investigators are analyzing CCTV footage from the estate to piece together the events.

za.headline: Democrats seize US Congress, vow investigations into Trump
za.dek: US President Donald Trump faces a hostile political landscape after Democrats won control of the House and Senate.
paragraphs: Democrats seized control of both the US House of Representatives and the Senate on Tuesday, ushering in a new political reality for President Donald Trump. The result leaves the 80-year-old president as a lame duck for his remaining two years in office. Democrats have vowed to launch investigations into Trump and his administration, focusing on accountability and affordability.

House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries stated that the "massive corruption" from the "Trump Cartel" has hindered progress for Americans and pledged immediate change. Vice President JD Vance publicly diverged from Trump, attributing the midterm losses to the Iran war. Trump acknowledged the war's impact on gasoline prices but defended the decision for long-term security.

Florida Governor Ron DeSantis described the defeat as an "extinction-level event" for Republicans in many areas. Trump, however, warned Democrats against impeachment attempts, predicting it would "destroy" their party. The US dollar and oil prices dropped on Wednesday following the election outcome, impacting global markets.

za.headline: South African police open over 120 criminal cases during elections
za.dek: Arrests made across the country for offences including fraud, assault, and contraventions of the Electoral Act.
paragraphs: South African Police Service (Saps) opened more than 120 criminal cases and arrested 59 people over three days of voting for the 2026 local government elections. The National Joint Operational and Intelligence Structure (Natjoints) reported these figures on Thursday, noting incidents occurred nationwide despite a focus on 331 high-risk voting stations. Police intervened to ensure voting continued at stations facing operational or logistical challenges.

KwaZulu-Natal (KZN) recorded the highest police activity with 18 cases and seven arrests, including eight contraventions of the Electoral Act and four intimidation cases. A police sergeant was removed from duty for arriving at a voting station with political party posters, and a burglary at Mnyameni High School involved the theft of sensitive IEC materials like ballot papers and the voters' roll. Acting KZN police commissioner Phumelele Makoba stated internal investigations are underway for these breaches.

Election day saw 57 cases opened and 27 arrests, with contraventions of the Electoral Act being the most frequent offence. Special voting days resulted in 65 cases and 32 arrests. Lieutenant General Tebello Mosikili confirmed police responsibility continues to protect voting materials and secure results. Police have also recorded 21 murder cases in recent months considered politically motivated.

za.headline: Cape Town dog impaled fleeing fireworks
za.dek: Max suffered fatal injuries trying to escape Guy Fawkes celebrations in Delft on November 5.
paragraphs: A Cape Town dog named Max died on Thursday, November 5, after being impaled on a security gate while trying to escape Guy Fawkes fireworks. Max panicked when fireworks began shortly after dark at his family’s home in Delft. His family had secured the gate, but he attempted to squeeze through the bars, sustaining severe injuries.

The Cape of Good Hope SPCA reported an 59% increase in calls on Guy Fawkes night, with 81 calls compared to 51 the previous year. Eight inspectors worked through the night, and at least five animals needed emergency veterinary care. SPCA communications manager Belinda Abraham stated Max should still be alive and urged residents to consider animals when celebrating with fireworks.

Veterinarians euthanised Max after a scan revealed extensive damage to his intestines and bladder. The SPCA is warning the public against donating to unverified animal rescue appeals, citing a recent social media appeal by Youth Pet Care founder Nazrudeen Adams that could not be verified. Residents can report distressed animals to the SPCA on 021 700 4158 or 021 700 4159.

ng.headline: INEC removes 1.27 million questionable voter records
ng.dek: Nigeria's electoral commission aims to prevent a repeat of 2023 presidential poll failures ahead of 2027.
paragraphs: Nigeria’s electoral commission has removed over 1.27 million questionable voter records from its register. The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) stated this action is part of efforts to address challenges that affected the 2023 presidential election. These measures are intended to improve processes for the 2027 general elections.

INEC Chairman Prof. Joash Ojo Amupitan met with traditional rulers in Kogi State on Thursday to seek their support for peaceful and credible elections. He visited Lokoja to assess the commission’s personnel and infrastructure preparedness for the 2027 general elections and an upcoming off-cycle governorship election. Amupitan also commissioned a storage facility for Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) devices at the INEC state headquarters.

The commission is committed to strengthening its operational capacity through infrastructure upgrades and technological tools for seamless electoral processes. Traditional rulers in Kogi State pledged to communicate the INEC chairman’s message to their subjects, assuring the commission of their dedication to peaceful, transparent, and credible elections in the state.

et.headline: 48 killed in Southeast Oromia armed attack
et.dek: Ethiopian Human Rights Commission confirms 20 injured, 247 households displaced and 21 houses destroyed.
paragraphs: 48 people died and 20 were injured in an armed attack on October 24, 2026, in Ethiopia's Southeast Oromia Zone. The Ethiopian Human Rights Commission (EHRC) reported that the OLF-Shene group attacked Birbona Chole Kebele, Sirka Woreda, destroying 21 houses and displacing 247 households. An undetermined number of cattle and sheep were also looted.

The EHRC investigation found the victims included 23 kebele security personnel, five militia members, and 20 civilians. The Commission gathered information from victims, families, eyewitnesses, and officials, verifying the killings through field and digital methods. EHRC Chief Commissioner Berhanu Adelo called the incident extremely serious and urged the government to strengthen civilian protection and improve early warning systems.

The Commission has repeatedly urged the government to prevent recurring attacks in the former Arsi Zone and bring perpetrators to justice. The EHRC is continuing investigations into human rights violations in Southeast Oromia and monitoring other regions including Gambella, the Oromia-Somali border, Amhara, and Tigray.

et.headline: China grants Ethiopia $15 million for railway parts
et.dek: The funds will support spare parts and technical assistance for the Ethio-Djibouti railway.
paragraphs: China has provided Ethiopia with a $15 million grant to supply spare parts and maintenance equipment for the Ethio-Djibouti railway. The agreement, signed in Addis Ababa on November 4, 2026, aims to enhance the reliability of this transport link. The grant will cover mechanical and electrical components for locomotives, track parts, and station accessories, along with machinery for inspection and maintenance.

Ethiopia’s State Minister of Finance, Tiguist Fisseha, and China’s Minister Counsellor Liu Xiaoguang signed the deal. The funding also includes technical assistance from Chinese experts to train railway staff and build local capacity. This support is intended to improve the railway's operational reliability and maintenance, particularly since Ethiopia and Djibouti took over management in May 2024.

The Ethio-Djibouti railway, which began operations in January 2018, is Ethiopia's main gateway to the sea. This grant builds on previous cooperation, including a five-year technical consultancy agreement signed in December 2025. Both nations pledged to coordinate the project's implementation for sustainable and efficient corridor operation.

et.headline: Ethiopian farmers learn soil and fertilizer innovations
et.dek: Field days in Southern Ethiopia from November 4 to 6, 2026, showcase digital tools and science-based practices.
paragraphs: The International Crops Research Institute for the Semi-Arid Tropics (ICRISAT) and partners are holding farmer field days in Southern Ethiopia from November 4 to 6, 2026. These events promote cost-effective ways to manage soil health and apply fertilizers, aiming to boost agricultural productivity.

Development organizations including Precision Development, People In Need, and Farm Africa are participating to inform farming communities about practical solutions. Farmers are experiencing science-based soil fertility management and learning about fertilizer advisory recommendations, including the AFER_LERSHA Telegram Bot.

The AFER_LERSHA (Soil for Farm) Telegram Bot offers farmers digital advice on fertilizer use tailored to their needs. This innovation helps farmers make informed decisions, optimize resource use, and achieve better yields at reduced costs.

et.headline: Ethiopia clashes push 50,000 into Kenya
et.dek: Fighting between Somali and Oromo communities over Moyale town has displaced tens of thousands seeking safety.
paragraphs: Deadly clashes between Ethiopian Somalis and Oromos over the town of Moyale have driven an estimated 50,000 people into neighbouring Kenya since October 18. The fighting, which has been ongoing daily, has made return home unsafe for the displaced.

The United Nations refugee agency (UNHCR) reports that at least 11,000 displaced individuals, primarily women and children, are now sheltered in temporary sites like schools. Others are being hosted by local communities in Kenya's border county, where two-thirds of residents live below the poverty line, straining local resources. Beshir Dadie Tufa, a father of three, told AFP the fighting continues daily and people are dying.
Conflict monitor ACLED has documented several deaths in the clashes, though an exact toll is difficult to confirm. Moyale itself is a town that straddles the border between Ethiopia and Kenya.

et.headline: AU steps up diplomacy to ease Ethiopia-Eritrea tensions
et.dek: Ambassador Bankole Adeoye calls for implementation of peace agreements and warns against escalation.
paragraphs: The African Union (AU) has intensified diplomatic efforts to reduce tensions between Ethiopia and Eritrea. AU Commissioner Bankole Adeoye stated the continental body is engaging leaders in both nations to prevent a full-blown crisis in the Horn of Africa. The AU is working to re-energize the Algiers and Pretoria Agreements, which address relations between Ethiopia and Eritrea and the conflict in Tigray, respectively.

Former Kenyan President Uhuru Kenyatta, the AU Chairperson’s High Representative for the Horn of Africa, is conducting consultations and shuttle diplomacy. Adeoye emphasized the AU's commitment to peace and collective security, condemning external interference that prolongs African conflicts. The AU Commission will continue engaging all parties to prevent the situation from developing into a full-scale crisis.

The AU is also strengthening its continent-wide approach to peacebuilding, focusing on conflict prevention. Leaders adopted new mechanisms in Luanda in August 2026 to identify emerging threats and address underlying causes, including climate shocks and geopolitical rivalries. The AU aims to advance Agenda 2063, envisioning a peaceful and prosperous continent.

gh.headline: Telecel Ghana Foundation helps over 500 patients go home
gh.dek: The Telecel Ghana Foundation's Homecoming initiative paid medical bills for insolvent patients at 16 government hospitals.
paragraphs: The Telecel Ghana Foundation launched its 2026 Homecoming initiative to help over 500 insolvent patients leave 16 government hospitals nationwide. The program began at Shai Osudoku District Hospital in Dodowa, where the Foundation paid the outstanding medical bills for 29 patients who were ready to go home. Telecel Ghana also provided National Health Insurance Scheme registration and renewal for 120 individuals.

Rita Agyeiwaa Rockson, who leads the Foundation, Sustainability and External Communications at Telecel Ghana, stated that the initiative aims to prevent financial hardship from keeping recovered patients from their families. Since 2011, Homecoming has assisted financially vulnerable patients and helped hospitals recover bills, freeing up beds. The Foundation also donated maternal-health equipment to Shai Osudoku District Hospital.

Dr Alexander Adjei, Medical Director of Shai Osudoku District Hospital, called the intervention a vital example of how partnerships can improve healthcare. Florence, a beneficiary, shared her relief after two weeks of uncertainty, wanting to return home to rest and care for herself and her baby.

gh.headline: Cenpower marks decade of Ghana power plant
gh.dek: The 350 MW Kpone Independent Power Plant has supplied electricity to one million households since 2019.
paragraphs: Cenpower Generation Ltd celebrated a decade since the sod-cutting ceremony for its 350 MW Kpone Independent Power Plant (KIPP). The event, themed “Powering Ghana’s Future Through Reliable and Sustainable Power Generation,” brought together government officials, shareholders, and energy sector stakeholders.

The company, incorporated in 2003 by four Ghanaian entrepreneurs, began developing KIPP to meet Ghana’s electricity demand. The project achieved financial close in December 2014, with sod-cutting on 29 January 2015, and commenced commercial operations on 10 June 2019.

Since beginning operations, KIPP has supplied enough electricity for about one million homes. Vice President Professor Jane Naana Opoku-Agyemang described Cenpower as an example of Ghanaian enterprise and private sector participation in national infrastructure development.

gh.headline: UN advocate calls for financial health council in Ghana
gh.dek: Queen Máxima urges coordinated efforts between government and private sector to boost citizen financial well-being.
paragraphs: Queen Máxima of the Netherlands, the UN Secretary-General’s Special Advocate for Financial Health, has called for Ghana to establish a Financial Health Council. This council would coordinate government and private sector actions aimed at improving the financial well-being of Ghanaians. She spoke in Accra at the joint inauguration of the Working Committee on the National Financial Inclusion and Development Strategy, which will develop a strategy for 2027 to 2031.

Queen Máxima stated that financial inclusion, while important, does not automatically lead to financial security or better livelihoods. She outlined four key components of financial health: managing daily finances, withstanding financial shocks, achieving long-term goals, and maintaining confidence in one's financial situation. Access to services like bank accounts, insurance, and pensions are part of this broader picture.

The committee is tasked with developing the strategy document for implementation between 2027 and 2031. Queen Máxima's call emphasizes that financial inclusion should serve as a means of achieving overall financial health and socio-economic development.

gh.headline: Ghana to track road crash data monthly
gh.dek: President Mahama will compare new TraffiTech system results with last year's figures to measure impact on deaths.
paragraphs: President John Dramani Mahama announced on Thursday, November 5, that Ghana will review road crash data monthly to assess the effectiveness of the new TraffiTech system. The government will compare accident figures recorded since the system began on November 1, 2026, with data from the same period last year. This review aims to measure the system's impact on reducing crashes and fatalities.

Speaking at Jubilee House, President Mahama urged motorists to adhere to speed limits, especially the 50-kilometre-per-hour limit in urban areas, as automated traffic enforcement increases. He expressed confidence that TraffiTech, which replaces manual police checks with automated speed detection, will significantly reduce road deaths. Last year, 2,151 people died in road crashes in Ghana, including 474 pedestrians, many of whom were schoolchildren.

The President stated that the speeding detection component is the only part of TraffiTech currently operational. He assured that a month-to-month comparison with last year's data would reveal surprising reductions in accidents and lives saved.

The SICs contribute about 40 per cent of the region's total revenue.

Discussions during the engagement addressed ECG's billing and payment systems, reasons for power outages and planned solutions, and the company's digital platforms for communication. The Accra West Regional Management team also visited over 70 SICs at their locations to acknowledge their partnership and contributions to ECG's growth. General Manager Mrs Sariel Adobea Etwire thanked customers for their consistent patronage and cooperation.

Mrs Etwire stated that staff are committed to providing prompt, responsive, and customer-focused services, emphasizing that going the extra mile is a commitment to delivering the best possible service. Some customers acknowledged ECG's efforts to improve service delivery and maintain dialogue with the business community.

cd.dek: The justice ministry aims to modernise the system with support from the EU and UNDP.
paragraphs: The Democratic Republic of Congo's Justice Ministry officially began digitalising judicial revenues and interconnecting justice services on Thursday, November 5, 2026. This initiative connects courts, public prosecutor offices, and penitentiary institutions across the country.

The reform, led by the Justice Ministry, receives technical assistance from the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) and financial backing from the European Union (EU). Officials stated the goal is to modernise the judicial system and improve citizen services.
This digitalisation process is intended to enhance transparency and streamline services for citizens interacting with the justice system. The project was launched in Kinshasa.

cd.headline: DR Congo rangers attack Ugandan goat herders
cd.dek: Tensions rise between Sarambwe reserve and Bwindi park communities after April goat seizure.
paragraphs: Tensions persist between communities bordering the Sarambwe Nature Reserve in DR Congo's Rutshuru territory and those near Uganda's Bwindi Impenetrable National Park. Local activist Muhindo Kibunga Elias reported on Thursday, November 5, that Ugandan eco-guards violently assaulted several Sarambwe community trackers on Monday.

The incident follows a dispute that began in April when Sarambwe trackers seized about 30 goats believed to belong to Ugandan herders inside the protected area. The goats were taken to a reserve surveillance post, and their owners are still seeking information on their fate from Sarambwe reserve managers.

Elias stated that the lack of clear explanations from reserve managers fuels the tensions, warning that the situation could escalate. He called for swift intervention from nature conservation authorities on both sides, urging the ICCN and Uganda Wildlife Authority to find a joint solution and involving the Greater Virunga Transboundary Collaboration.
