paragraphs: The Academy of Fine Arts in Kinshasa organized a scientific conference on Wednesday, November 4, focusing on the conservation and restoration of artworks. The event aimed to foster dialogue between indigenous knowledge and contemporary practices in art preservation.

tz.headline: Tanzania invites Algerian firms to explore investment
tz.dek: Ambassador Mobhare Matinyi seeks partnerships in agriculture, energy, pharmaceuticals, construction, and manufacturing.
paragraphs: Tanzania is seeking to translate its friendship with Algeria into stronger commercial partnerships, inviting Algerian companies to explore investment opportunities across agriculture, energy, pharmaceuticals, construction, and manufacturing. Tanzania’s Ambassador to Algeria, Mobhare Matinyi, made the appeal during the Embassy’s monthly press briefing in Algiers on Monday. The initiative aims to inform the public about emerging opportunities for trade, investment, and technical collaboration.

Ambassador Matinyi highlighted potential collaboration in agriculture and agro-processing, noting Algeria's advances in food processing and export readiness. He engaged with Algerian companies involved in food processing, meat, and chicken production, encouraging investment in Tanzania. Opportunities were also presented in livestock technologies, animal health, feed production, fertilizers, irrigation, and food packaging.

The Embassy's engagements followed participation in the "Made in Algeria" Agri-Food Trade Fair on October 17, where Tanzania identified companies whose capabilities could support national priorities. Both countries occupy strategic positions, with Algeria linking North Africa and the Sahel, and Tanzania connecting East, Central, and Southern African markets representing over 500 million people.

tz.headline: Tanzania youth leader charged with counselling terrorism
tz.dek: CHADEMA official Coletha Clavery Ntidyicha faces charges of advising the public to commit terrorist acts.
paragraphs: Coletha Clavery Ntidyicha, 31, chairperson of CHADEMA’s youth wing BAVICHA in Kigoma Region, was charged with counselling terrorist acts at the Kisutu Resident Magistrate’s Court in Dar es Salaam. The charge sheet, dated November 3, 2026, alleges she advised the public to participate in acts causing serious property damage to destabilise the country’s structures between August 1 and October 23, 2026.

CHADEMA stated on November 4 that Ntidyicha was brought to court without her lawyers present, alleging denial of legal access. The charge sheet, under the Prevention of Terrorism Act, does not specify the words used, the communication method, or the property targeted. Ntidyicha was arrested on October 14 in Temeke, and her detention became the subject of a High Court application.

CHADEMA’s communications director, Brenda Rupia, said on November 4 that the party supports the rule of law but believes terrorism charges are used to silence opponents. A High Court application concerning Ntidyicha's whereabouts had previously overcome a government objection regarding a defective affidavit on October 28, allowing an additional affidavit to be considered.

tz.headline: Tanzania hosts African seed sector talks
tz.dek: Dar es Salaam will convene African Union states and agricultural stakeholders from November 10-13 to improve seed access and food security.
paragraphs: Tanzania will host a four-day meeting in Dar es Salaam from November 10-13 to discuss transforming Africa’s seed sector. The gathering will bring together African Union member states and agricultural stakeholders to improve access to quality planting materials and advance food security across the continent.

The event comprises the seventh Steering Group Meeting and third General Assembly of the African Seed and Biotechnology Partnership Platform (ASB PP), convened by the African Union Development Agency-NEPAD (AUDA-NEPAD) and the African Union Commission (AUC). Representatives from regional economic communities, research institutions, farmers’ organizations, private-sector actors, development partners, and civil society will attend.

Discussions will focus on strengthening the partnership platform's effectiveness, reviewing the implementation of the African Seed and Biotechnology Programme (ASBP), and identifying priority interventions. Key priorities include implementing the ASBP 10-year action plan, advancing the Farmer-Managed Seed Systems Framework, and harmonising regional seed policies.

tz.headline: CAF delegation praises Tanzania's 2027 AFCON readiness
tz.dek: Inspectors noted progress on stadiums and infrastructure, with playing surfaces showing visible growth.
paragraphs: A Confederation of African Football (CAF) delegation, led by General Secretary Samson Adamu, expressed satisfaction with Tanzania’s progress in preparing to host the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations. The inspectors visited infrastructure in Dar es Salaam, Zanzibar, and Arusha, acknowledging advancements toward meeting tournament requirements.

Leodegar Tenga, chairman of the AFCON Local Organising Committee, reported that nearly all commitments to CAF are met, with ongoing work on stadium enhancements, particularly the playing surfaces. Grass has been planted and is expected to grow visibly within two to three weeks, addressing a key area of focus.

Improvements to access roads near stadiums are also in progress, with the Tanzania National Roads Agency (TANROADS) involved. Hospitality facilities for dignitaries are being built, alongside considerations for ordinary fans, visiting families, and football tourists to ensure a positive experience and promote Tanzania's tourism.

tz.headline: CRDB Bank enhances digital services
tz.dek: Customers can now self-register for internet banking and unlock accounts without visiting a branch.
paragraphs: CRDB Bank has upgraded its internet banking services in Dar es Salaam, introducing systems for faster, easier, and more secure transactions. Customers can now register for the service themselves, eliminating the need to visit a bank branch.

Bonaventure Paul, CRDB Bank's Director of Customer Service, stated that these improvements aim to remove challenges for internet banking users and boost efficiency. The service now operates 24 hours a day, seven days a week, allowing customers to access banking services anytime.

A key enhancement is the self-registration system for customers with a CRDB account linked to an ATM card. Additionally, customers can now unlock their internet banking accounts if they enter the wrong password multiple times, without needing to visit a branch for verification.

ma.headline: Morocco allocates MAD 400 million in transport subsidies
ma.dek: Government aims to shield consumers from rising fuel costs with increased direct payments to transport operators.
paragraphs: Morocco will provide MAD 400 million in direct subsidies to road transport professionals, supporting approximately 200,000 vehicles. Transport Minister Abdessamad Kayouh announced on Thursday that this new allocation is a 60% increase over the initial subsidy tranche. Payments will be disbursed every 15 days, starting November 10, to offset rising fuel prices and their impact on transport fares and consumer goods.

The subsidy is intended to absorb energy cost increases affecting passenger transport and the movement of essential goods, according to Minister Kayouh. He urged transport operators not to raise official fares, stating the financial support aims to protect end consumers and maintain logistics sector stability. The support applies to vehicles registered with the Transport Ministry and NARSA that meet eligibility criteria.

Government spokesperson Samir Belfkih stated that protecting household purchasing power is a strategic priority, with measures to increase incomes and curb inflation. The government is also preparing legislation to create six regional companies next year to organize markets and regulate distribution, addressing intermediaries who account for nearly 70% of some product prices. The government has ruled out capping fuel company profits or reducing fuel taxes.

ma.dek: Fatima Zahra Chaaba named director at the Ministry of Justice, among other key roles filled.
paragraphs: Morocco’s government approved appointments to senior positions across several ministries and public institutions on Thursday. Taoufik Mediani was appointed director of Legislation on Governance, Rights and Freedoms at the General Secretariat of the Government.

In economic sectors, Yassine Ahmimi was appointed director of Statistics, Studies, Monitoring and Evaluation at the Ministry of Industry, Trade, Investment and Economic Integration. Chafik Ssalouh was named director of Customs Control and Investigations at the Customs and Indirect Tax Administration. Safaa Reddaf was appointed director of Civil Aviation at the Ministry of Transport and Logistics.

Hafida Khouyi was appointed director of the National Higher Institute of Music and Choreographic Arts at the Ministry of Youth, Culture and Sports. El Houcine Haida was appointed director of the Skhirat-Temara Urban Agency, and Hicham El Khersani was named director of the Rabat-Salé Urban Agency. Said Kobra’s appointment as director of the Errachidia-Midelt Urban Agency was renewed.

ma.headline: Morocco secures US$112 million loan for port strategy
ma.dek: The French Development Agency loan will fund infrastructure, renewable energy, and fishing port modernization until 2030.
paragraphs: Morocco's National Ports Agency has secured US$112 million in financing from the French Development Agency (AFD) for its 2023-2030 investment programme. The 13-year loan, signed in Rabat on November 3, 2026, will support upgrades to port infrastructure, renewable energy and desalination facilities, fishing ports, and port quay electrification.

The financing specifically targets ports in southern Morocco, including Tan-Tan, Tarfaya, Laâyoune, Boujdour, Dakhla, and Lamhiriz, aiming to boost regional economic development and strengthen the country's Atlantic coast position. This loan is structured as a non-sovereign loan, placing repayment risk on the agency rather than the Moroccan government.

Moroccan ports processed 262.6 million tonnes of cargo in 2025, an increase of 8.9% from 241.2 million tonnes in 2024, with Tanger Med handling 10.3 million TEUs. The development of southern ports like Dakhla and Laâyoune is intended to capture transit trade with Sahel economies, a market currently served by West African ports.

ma.headline: Morocco prison population exceeds 102,000
ma.dek: Overcrowding reaches 158% as prison chief urges judges to reduce pretrial detentions.
paragraphs: Morocco's prisons held 102,941 inmates by the end of October, a rise from 98,692 a year prior, according to prison chief Mohamed Saleh Tamek. The national occupancy rate now stands at 158%, with some facilities exceeding 300% capacity. This strain impacts basic services, security, and daily operations.

Tamek informed lawmakers on Wednesday that the increasing inmate numbers are a primary obstacle to improving prison conditions. The growing population also burdens infrastructure, equipment, and staff, while escalating operating costs. He urged judicial authorities to decrease reliance on pretrial detention and utilize alternative sentences more effectively.

Despite legal reforms and the application of alternative sentences to 3,408 individuals between January and September, the prison population continues to grow. Automatic sentence reductions have benefited 152,487 cases, leading to 12,547 releases, but these measures are insufficient to curb the trend. Tamek stated that addressing the factors driving the growing number of people entering the prison system is necessary, not just expanding capacity or releasing inmates.

The attack occurred during a period when Algeria was experiencing its own civil war, known as the Black Decade, between 1991 and 2002. This conflict pitted the Algerian government and army against Islamist groups.
Morocco had been spared the violence of Islamist terrorism prior to this 1994 incident, contrasting with the ongoing conflict in neighboring Algeria.

ug.headline: Deaf Link Uganda director shot dead in Kisoro lodge attack
ug.dek: Unidentified gunmen killed Barbra Nassozi Kiyaga, 58, during a suspected robbery attempt at Mucha Lodge.
paragraphs: The founding executive director of Deaf Link Uganda, Barbra Nassozi Kiyaga, was shot dead during a gun attack at Mucha Lodge in Kisoro district early on Thursday. Unidentified gunmen attacked the lodge near River Mucha at about 2 am, in what police suspect was an attempted robbery. The assailants exchanged fire with security guards, resulting in Kiyaga's death and injuring Police Constable Charles Mukesi.

Kigezi Region police spokesperson Nelson Tumushime stated that Kiyaga, a Kampala resident, had checked into the lodge on Wednesday for a four-day stay. She died at the scene and her body was taken to Kisoro Hospital for a postmortem. Constable Mukesi sustained a gunshot wound to his left leg and is receiving treatment in stable condition at Kisoro Hospital. Police have launched an operation to find the attackers and have increased security in the area.

This incident follows two other killings in Kisoro district within the past month. Prominent businessman Africano Nteziyaremye and his wife Peace Kyompeire were shot dead on October 17, 2026. A week prior, suspected gunmen attacked Bweza Lodge in an apparent robbery attempt. Police have not yet established a connection between these incidents or the motive for Kiyaga's killing.

ug.headline: Ugandan coffee firms debut at Swiss festival
ug.dek: Gorilla Conservation Coffee and Carico Coffee sold products directly to 5,500 visitors at Zurich's largest coffee trade fair.
paragraphs: Ugandan coffee companies Gorilla Conservation Coffee and Carico Coffee participated in the Swiss Coffee Festival in Zurich from October 31 to November 1. This marked Uganda’s first appearance at Switzerland’s largest coffee trade fair, which drew about 5,500 visitors and 78 exhibitors. The companies offered tastings, met potential buyers, and sold their products directly to consumers in an effort to capture more value from their crop.

Uganda’s Ambassador to Switzerland Marcel Tibaleka stated, “We are delighted to introduce more of Uganda’s exceptional coffee brands to Swiss consumers and look forward to building lasting partnerships.” The embassy in Switzerland secured the stand for the two companies, supporting efforts to expand coffee exports and promote value addition. Carico Coffee purchases directly from approximately 1,700 smallholder farmers in the Mount Elgon region.

Uganda shipped 8.8 million 60kg bags of coffee worth $2.4 billion in the 12 months to March 2026, though over 98 percent leaves the country as unroasted green beans. The government launched a national coffee brand, “Uganda Coffee: It’s in Our Nature,” in June and aims for production exceeding 20 million bags annually by 2030. About 1.7 million Ugandan households depend on coffee for their livelihoods.

ug.headline: Uganda court extends indecent assault protection to men
ug.dek: Constitutional Court rules existing laws are discriminatory and orders government to propose amendments.
paragraphs: Uganda's Constitutional Court has extended legal protection against indecent assault and acts insulting modesty to men, ruling that provisions of the Penal Code Act previously protecting only women and girls are discriminatory. The court, sitting in Kampala, also declared unconstitutional provisions of the Magistrates Courts Act that allow magistrates to investigate cases, formulate charges, and then preside over the trial.

A panel of five justices, led by Justice Cheborion Barishaki, unanimously ordered that the words “any woman or girl” in Section 115(1) and (3) of the Penal Code Act be replaced with “any person.” This ruling followed consolidated petitions filed by city lawyer Steven Kalali, Pader District Chief Magistrate Martins Kirya, and lawyer Michael Aboneka.

The petitioners argued that restricting protection against indecent assault and acts insulting modesty to women and girls discriminated against men, contravening Article 21 of the Constitution. The Attorney General defended the provisions as affirmative action for women, but the court rejected this, stating that while women need protection, the law cannot deny men equivalent protection against similar harm.

ug.headline: Uganda shilling hits record low against dollar
ug.dek: The Uganda shilling has weakened by about 12% against the US dollar, pushing up the cost of living.
paragraphs: The Uganda shilling is at a record low against the US dollar, depreciating by about 12% and increasing the cost of living. Imports are now more expensive, impacting industries reliant on foreign materials and driving up prices for essential goods like fuel. The dollar now costs over 4400 shillings, making a liter of gas approximately 7000 UGX.

This currency weakness benefits a minority of exporters but squeezes households and small businesses, which form the backbone of Uganda's economy. The Bank of Uganda raised interest rates to 12% in October to combat inflation, which stood at nearly 5% in September.

The price of a loaf of bread is set to rise from 5000 UGX to 8000 UGX due to increased wheat costs. Transport fares have also increased, with a 1000 UGX journey now costing 1500 UGX or more, affecting families on fixed incomes.

ug.headline: Uganda finance professionals to convene on tech and AI
ug.dek: The fifth ACCA Uganda Members Convention on November 19-20 will gather accountants and leaders to discuss profession-wide changes.
paragraphs: Finance and accounting professionals will gather in Kampala for the fifth ACCA Uganda Members Convention on November 19 and 20, 2026. The two-day event at Speke Resort and Convention Centre will focus on how technology, artificial intelligence, and evolving business demands are reshaping the profession. Organised by ACCA Uganda, the convention's theme is “Navigating Change: Flexible and Inclusive Career Pathways.”

The convention will convene accountants, business leaders, policymakers, ACCA members, affiliates, and students to discuss adapting to automation, AI, data-driven business, and global standards. Finance Minister Henry Musasizi is expected to officiate the opening, while National Planning Authority Executive Director Dr Joseph Muvawala will discuss accountants' role in Uganda’s growth. Speakers will also cover global opportunities and sustainability reporting.

Discussions will include AI in public financial management, Uganda’s sustainability roadmap, IFRS S1 and S2 adoption, green finance, and carbon markets. Topics also cover labour market changes, digital transformation, talent management, professional wellbeing, and mentorship. ACCA Uganda Country Manager Charlotte Kukunda stated the event will help professionals examine changes impacting their work and businesses.

zw.headline: Cold Storage Company trebles cattle slaughter rate
zw.dek: Zimbabwe's state-run beef giant shows recovery after US$9.3 million rescue from Mutapa Investment Fund.
paragraphs: Zimbabwe's Cold Storage Company (CSC) has tripled its daily cattle slaughter rate from 50 to 150 head. This recovery follows a US$9.3 million cash injection last year from its parent company, the Mutapa Investment Fund.

The Bulawayo-based processor's refrigeration facilities can now accommodate 320 carcasses. Minister of Lands, Agriculture, Fisheries, Water and Rural Development, Dr Anxious Masuka, visited the facility and noted its progress towards a processing capacity of 800 beasts a day.

CSC, formed in 1937, once handled up to 150,000 tonnes of beef a year and exported to the EU. Its decline began in 1992, accelerating in 2001 when the EU suspended imports after a Foot and Mouth Disease outbreak, leading to debts over US$25 million.

zw.headline: Bata Group targets Zimbabwe for regional footwear exports
zw.dek: The global shoe manufacturer identified skills development and local sourcing as priorities for its new hub.
paragraphs: Bata Group has identified Zimbabwe as a potential centre for regional footwear manufacturing and export. The company's global chief executive, Panos Mytaros, met President Emmerson Mnangagwa to discuss the plan. Mytaros stated that skills development, improved product quality, and local sourcing are key priorities for the initiative.

Mytaros indicated that Bata Group sees opportunities for growth within Zimbabwe. The company aims to leverage local capabilities to enhance its manufacturing output and expand its reach across the region. This strategic move signals a significant investment in Zimbabwe's industrial sector.

The Bata Group's focus on developing local skills and increasing product quality is expected to boost the country's manufacturing capacity and potentially lead to increased employment and economic activity.

cv.headline: Mindelact festival returns to Cape Verde
cv.dek: The 32nd edition of the international theatre festival runs until Saturday with daily shows on São Vicente island.
paragraphs: The 32nd Mindelact International Theatre Festival began today in São Vicente, Cape Verde, and will run until Saturday. The festival, organised by the association Mindelact, features daily performances at the Centro Cultural do Mindelo, with the opening show being "Amontoados," a co-production between Portugal's Teatro Griot and Mindelact.

The festival's theme, "Edição Raiz," celebrates Cape Verdean cultural roots and the 90th anniversary of the Movimento Claridade. Vice-president José Pedro Bettencourt stated in October that the event aims to reinforce the archipelago's identity while maintaining an international dimension, with participants from Portugal, Spain, Brazil, Togo, Italy, and Denmark. Organisers noted persistent challenges, including a lack of venues, which have caused discouragement and led some founders to leave.

Founded in 1995 with only island-based groups, Mindelact expanded nationally in 1996 and internationally in 1997. The organisation describes Mindelact as Cape Verde's primary theatre event and the most significant in Lusophone Africa. The programme also includes encounters, workshops, and events in Praia and Porto Novo.

td.headline: Chad officials review local investment priorities
td.dek: Moundou hosts annual meeting to improve public investment planning and territorial development.
paragraphs: Officials in Moundou, Chad, met from November 4 to 6, 2026, to review the Annual Investment Programme (PAI). The meeting, organised by the ministries of Finance and Territorial Administration, aimed to strengthen territorial planning and boost public investment efficiency for local populations.

The review focused on improving public investment planning and programming, with attention to local development needs. Yahya Mahamadou Bellout, Director of Cabinet for the Logone Occidental Governorate, stated that PAI's effectiveness depends on accurate needs identification, resource availability, realistic objectives, and rigorous project monitoring.

The meeting also addressed the challenge of translating plans into concrete actions. Solkam Bachir Soucat, head of the mission, highlighted that PAI instruments help align local priorities with the national development plan and Sustainable Development Goals, reinforcing accountability of autonomous collectivités and improving citizen input in public decisions.

dj.headline: Djibouti launches emergency medical service
dj.dek: The new SAMU aims to bring hospital care to patients when emergencies demand it.
paragraphs: Djibouti has launched a new emergency medical service, SAMU, following a week of training with Hospices civils de Lyon. The service will operate with medical regulation, mobile teams, and adapted transport, focusing on permanence, resilience to disasters, and territorial equity.

Health Minister Mouna Osman Aden, who led the launch ceremony, stated the ambition is to "bring the hospital to the patient when the emergency demands it." The initiative involves the University Hospital, the National Social Security Fund, and the Military Hospital, which presented its mass casualty preparedness plan.

The SAMU's operational framework includes three commitments: constant availability, resilience in the face of catastrophes, and equitable access across the country. Minister Aden emphasized that "no Djiboutian should be less protected because they live far from a hospital."

paragraphs: Djibouti's first Beach Festival opened on November 5, 2026, on Heron beach, with the Minister of Commerce and Tourism, Orbis Helaf Orbis, presiding over the launch ceremony. The event, running until November 7, aims to highlight Djibouti's coastline and the potential of its youth. It includes cultural, sports, and economic activities, alongside stands for artisans and young entrepreneurs.

Organized by IN'PACT Social under the institutional sponsorship of the Ministry of Commerce and Tourism, the festival is designed to be a showcase for local creativity and the opportunities presented by the country's maritime facade. Government officials, including the president of the Ports and Free Zones Authority and the prefect of Djibouti-ville, Abdi Hassan Ahmed, attended the opening.

Authorities intend for this initiative to promote national maritime heritage, stimulate tourism, and provide a new platform for local talents. The festival's theme, 'Djibouti Blue Generation,' underscores the focus on engaging and empowering the nation's young people.

dj.headline: Djibouti agency and French development bank review urban projects
dj.dek: The Agence Djiboutienne de Développement Social and the French Development Agency visited Balbala to inspect completed and ongoing urban development works.
paragraphs: The Agence Djiboutienne de Développement Social (ADDS) and the French Development Agency (AFD) reviewed urban development projects in Djibouti. AFD director Mme Belliot visited the ADDS technical teams to see progress on the Integrated Urban Development Project (PDUI2 Ter) and the Shebelley Technical Landfill Centre. The landfill project is co-financed by AFD and the European Union for 16 million euros.

In the Balbala district, the delegation inspected facilities completed under PDUI2, including a gendarmerie brigade, market halls, sports fields, and a Community Development Centre. They also observed ongoing work for PDUI2 Ter, which continues urban transformation in the area. ADDS Director General highlighted the long-standing partnership with AFD and thanked French taxpayers for their contribution to projects totaling 24 million euros.

Mme Belliot praised the ADDS teams for their work quality on the projects. These initiatives are part of the 'Zero Slum' Programme, led by the Ministry of City, aiming for inclusive and sustainable urban development for residents.

sz.headline: SEL gives E600 000 to Eswatini charities
sz.dek: The investment holding company distributed funds to education, children's welfare, and cancer care initiatives.
paragraphs: Swazi Empowerment Limited (SEL) has donated E600 000 to three Eswatini institutions supporting education infrastructure, vulnerable children, and cancer care. The investment holding company, listed on the Eswatini Stock Exchange, provided the financial support through its Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) programme. Beneficiary institutions included the Ministry of Education and Training, SOS Children’s Village, and Eswatini Cancer Network.

SEL CSR Chairperson Shaka Ndlangamandla stated that the funding comes from dividends generated by the company’s investments. He explained that this demonstrates how corporate returns can address social development needs. Representatives from the recipient organisations expressed gratitude, noting the timely assistance amid financial difficulties faced by NGOs.

The Ministry of Education and Training highlighted the donation's importance for addressing school infrastructure challenges, such as rehabilitating dilapidated facilities. Principal Economist Nkululeko Gwebu noted SEL's long-standing partnership with the ministry, which has previously funded school construction and water provision.

sz.headline: Nearly half of police homes unfit
sz.dek: Royal Eswatini Police Service reports deteriorating housing and accommodation shortages affect officers.
paragraphs: Almost half of police residential properties in Eswatini have been declared unfit for human occupation, according to the Royal Eswatini Police Service (REPS). Health and environmental officials made the declaration during the second quarter of the 2026/27 financial year, which ran from July to September 2026.

REPS stated that deteriorating housing and accommodation shortages have led to officers sharing facilities, causing disputes and health risks. The service acknowledges that the affected buildings require urgent repairs or replacement, impacting officer welfare and operations. Planned repairs include work at the Police Academy kitchen and bat waste removal from ceilings at facilities in Tshaneni, Big Bend, Lavumisa, Simunye, Lomahasha, and Lubulini.

The government allocated E15.75 million for rehabilitation and security fencing, but REPS considers this insufficient. Additional funding of E13.125 million was received for institutional housing projects in Mbabane, Lubulini, and Hlane, with some units completed but awaiting handover. Financial and administrative challenges, including potential contractor payment delays, could affect planned policing programmes.

sz.headline: MP says pastors' divorces fuel rising divorce cases
sz.dek: Eswatini MP Tanele Magagula links church leaders' marital issues to family breakdown and questions their guidance.
paragraphs: Hhohho Region Member of Parliament Tanele Magagula stated in Parliament that pastors losing their mandate may be contributing to rising divorce cases in Eswatini. She expressed concern that some pastors are themselves divorcing, questioning who will guide couples if religious leaders fail to uphold marriage values. Magagula believes this failure means couples are not adequately guided on resolving marital disagreements.

During a debate on the Ministry of Home Affairs’ performance report, Magagula noted that pastors' personal divorces raise questions about their ability to teach couples how to handle marriages. She argued that some pastors no longer preach marriage fundamentals or the importance of strong family structures. This lack of guidance leads to disputes being taken to court instead of being resolved within families.

The MP also criticized the erosion of family involvement in marriage arrangements, citing modern practices where only pastors and a few church members are involved. Magagula questioned how church members, unfamiliar with couples' backgrounds, could offer adequate guidance. She also warned about mushrooming churches that allegedly preach against families and discourage involvement with relatives in marriage matters.

ga.headline: Gabon seeks Chinese investment for industrialisation
ga.dek: President Oligui Nguema invited Chinese investors to the Nkok special economic zone on November 5, 2026.
paragraphs: Gabon's President Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguema urged Chinese investors to develop local processing of raw materials during the 9th China International Import Expo (CIIE) in Shanghai on November 5, 2026. Gabon, the guest of honour, participated with a national pavilion for the first time, aiming to attract industrial partnerships. The president stated that Gabon is a platform for investment to build a new future.

Speaking as the only African president at the opening ceremony, Nguema highlighted the long-standing friendship between China and Gabon and the concrete results of their trade agreements. He invited investors to the Nkok special economic zone, describing it as a strategic gateway to Central Africa with 200 million consumers. He also pointed to opportunities in timber, manganese, iron, energy, water, health, digital, and agriculture sectors, noting five million hectares of arable land.

The Gabonese leader presented Gabon as offering political stability, legal security, a new investment code, free profit transfer, and reforms in labour, mining, and petroleum codes. He mentioned the digitalisation of administration, allowing for online company creation in 48 hours. The expo showcased local products and highlighted Gabon's potential in green economy, carbon credits, renewable energy, and pharmacopoeia.

ga.headline: Gabon president visits Shanghai robot valley
ga.dek: Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguema seeks to position Gabon in global tech revolution by integrating AI and robotics.
paragraphs: Gabon's President Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguema visited the Zhangjiang Robot Valley in Shanghai on November 4, 2026, expressing a desire for the nation to actively participate in the global technological revolution. He aims to integrate artificial intelligence into public services and promote robotization, ensuring Gabon is part of this transformation rather than a passive observer.

During his visit, President Oligui Nguema observed robots performing surgical procedures, patient rehabilitation, and managing industrial operations, noting that this is current reality, not science fiction. He emphasized the urgency of preparing young Gabonese for these emerging technologies, stating, "Gabon will not watch this revolution from afar."

Gabon is already taking steps toward digital transformation, including the completion of preparatory work for its first national Artificial Intelligence Strategy on September 30, supported by the UNDP. The country also inaugurated its first national Data Center in Nkok on July 3, 2026, a Tier III certified facility designed to host and secure strategic data within the nation.

ga.headline: Gabon aviation fees rise 7.97%
ga.dek: Aviation revenue reached 1.547 billion FCFA by September 2026, up from the previous year.
paragraphs: Aviation fees in Gabon generated 1.547 billion FCFA by September 2026, an increase of 7.97% compared to the same period in 2025. Other operating revenues also grew to 316 million FCFA, a 5.93% rise. These figures were presented on November 4, 2026, in Libreville during the 46th session on national aviation activities.

The overall budget realization rate stood at 59.2% as of September 30, 2026. Joachim Tchissambou M’Boundou, cabinet chief for Asecna Gabon's director general, reported that out of 12 decisions reviewed, four were fully executed, four are in progress, three partially executed, and one remains unexecuted. Two recommendations have not been acted upon.

Beyond financial indicators, participants discussed improving aviation service quality, safety, and continuity. The partnership between Gabon and Asecna, based on a management delegation contract signed on February 5, 2019, emphasizes shared responsibility. Enhancing airport facilities and ensuring decisions are implemented are priorities for strengthening public aviation services.

ga.headline: Gabon ex-PM questioned over detention
ga.dek: Alain-Claude Bilie-By-Nze faced his judge for the first time since his April 16 arrest.
paragraphs: Former Gabonese Prime Minister Alain-Claude Bilie-By-Nze was questioned by an investigating judge in Libreville on Thursday, November 5. Assisted by his lawyer, Me Sarah-Ognyane, Bilie-By-Nze appeared before the judge for the first time since his preventive detention began on April 16. The hearing followed months of requests from his defense team.

The interrogation, which started at 9 a.m., focused on statements previously made by a woman named Baba Ramatou on April 27. Me Sarah-Ognyane stated that her client provided clarifications on the accusations against him and described the proceedings as having gone "very well." The lawyer deemed the audition late but necessary for respecting the defense's rights.

The next steps in the procedure may include a confrontation between Bilie-By-Nze and Baba Ramatou, followed by a moral investigation and defense submissions. The judge will then decide whether to dismiss the case, leading to Bilie-By-Nze's release, or to send him to trial. His lawyer reported that Bilie-By-Nze is in good physical and psychological condition despite his detention.

gm.headline: Gambia reports trade gains but potential untapped
gm.dek: The Gambia and LDC Group saw export earnings rise, but primary products still dominate.
paragraphs: The global trading system has delivered measurable gains for The Gambia, including market access, export earnings, economic activity, and jobs, according to Ambassador Muhammadou M.O. Kah. Speaking in Geneva on October 29, 2026, on behalf of Trade Minister Mod Ceesay, Kah stated that trade is a foreign-exchange lifeline for The Gambia, with merchandise exports reaching USD 407 million and commercial services exports USD 479 million in 2025.

Tourism and travel alone accounted for 91.6 per cent of The Gambia's services exports in 2024, highlighting the need for diversification and value addition. Ambassador Kah also noted that regional integration, through the OMVG interconnection, has provided The Gambia with lower-cost electricity from Guinea, saving its utility, NAWEC, an estimated 42 per cent and helping it return to profitability. For the wider LDC Group, merchandise exports rose to USD 313 billion in 2025, and commercial services exports reached USD 53.1 billion.

Despite these gains, primary products still accounted for 53 per cent of LDC merchandise exports in 2025, with 10 exporters generating 71 per cent of the total. Ambassador Kah stressed that market access alone is insufficient, and productive capacity, infrastructure, standards, and competitiveness are crucial. He outlined priorities for The Gambia and other LDCs, including value addition in agro-processing and fisheries, climate-resilient sectors, and green and digital industries.

gm.headline: Dumbuya promises D2,000 rent if elected
gm.dek: Democratic Party leader Yusupha A. Dumbuya faced questions from the IEC over missing nomination documents.
paragraphs: Democratic Party leader Yusupha A. Dumbuya pledged to cap rent for a two-bedroom house at D2,000 if elected president. He also proposed D4,000 for a three-bedroom house, with government subsidies to support the plan. Dumbuya presented his nomination papers to the Independent Electoral Commission (IEC) on Wednesday.

IEC Chairman Joseph Colley raised concerns about Dumbuya’s nomination, noting the absence of his voter’s card and Senior Secondary School Certificate. The commission also questioned the proof of payment for the D1 million nomination fee and inconsistencies in his name. Dumbuya’s nomination is pending verification of these requirements.

Dumbuya also criticized the government for failing to deliver a new constitution and promised to implement constitutional term limits. Former Vice President Dr. Isatou Touray also filed her nomination as an independent candidate for the December 5 presidential election.

gm.headline: African universities strengthen child rights resolve
gm.dek: Gambia hosts meeting to boost research, policy, and collaboration for children's welfare across Africa.
paragraphs: African universities, government officials, and UN representatives convened in Banjul for the Second Meeting of the African Network of Universities for Child Rights. The gathering aimed to validate the network's governance, expand membership, and boost collaboration to advance children's rights across the continent.

University of The Gambia Vice Chancellor Professor Herbert Robinson called the meeting a historic milestone, highlighting the university's new Child Rights Centre, supported by UNICEF. He stressed that universities must lead research, policy influence, and evidence generation to improve children's lives, especially those in vulnerable communities.

The UN reaffirmed its commitment to the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child and the African Charter on the Rights and Welfare of the Child. With less than four years to the 2030 Sustainable Development Goals, the meeting focused on generating locally owned, evidence-based policies and strengthening child rights education and advocacy.

gn.headline: Guinea president lists 92 occupational diseases
gn.dek: President Mamadi Doumbouya established a decree on November 5, 2026, detailing compensable professional illnesses.
paragraphs: President Mamadi Doumbouya has established a framework for compensating occupational diseases in Guinea. A decree released on Thursday, November 5, 2026, lists 92 professional illnesses eligible for compensation. This regulation defines the legal and technical basis for recognizing these conditions and creates a specialized body to monitor and update the list.

The decree categorizes these illnesses into four main groups: those caused by chemical agents, physical agents, biological agents, and those affecting specific organs or functions. Each table within the decree's annex is structured with three columns to guide doctors, employers, and social security organizations in determining compensation rights.

This measure aims to strengthen social protection for Guinean workers. The decree also establishes a mechanism for the ongoing monitoring and updating of the list of compensable professional diseases.

gn.headline: Guinean man freed after six months in jail for theft
gn.dek: Amadou Diallo was acquitted by the Dixinn court on November 5, 2026, for a crime he denied committing.
paragraphs: Amadou Diallo walked free on Thursday, November 5, 2026, after spending over six months in prison. He was detained on April 24, 2026, accused of theft by his neighbor, Mamadou Bobo Diallo. The Dixinn Court of First Instance found Amadou Diallo not guilty of the charges, stating the offense was not constituted.

Amadou Diallo told the court he had only climbed a wall to enter his own home when he was arrested. The public prosecutor, Mamadou Yaya Fatoumata Boiro, had requested a one-year sentence, with six months suspended, believing Diallo was guilty because he was apprehended in the complainant's yard at night. The court, however, did not follow the prosecution's recommendation.

Amadou Diallo explained that an altercation occurred after he climbed the fence and was questioned by his neighbor. The neighborhood chief intervened, and the dispute was brought before the court. The verdict means Amadou Diallo is released from detention.

gn.headline: Guinean school director says paid tutoring is indispensable
gn.dek: Mohamed Mara states that extra lessons help students grasp difficult concepts and improve grades.
paragraphs: Mohamed Mara, director of the Excellence Moussa Traoré school in N’Zérékoré, stated that paid tutoring is indispensable for students' academic success. He explained that while school provides the foundation, parents must arrange for private tutors to help students excel. Mara noted that different students learn at different paces, and some require repeated explanations to understand lessons taught in class.

Mara acknowledged that some parents hesitate due to the costs associated with tutoring, but he believes the benefits outweigh the expenses. He mentioned that some teachers offer affordable rates, though not all parents recognize the value of these supplementary lessons. The school director also highlighted that his institution offers free tutoring, but attendance is a challenge, with some students citing household chores as a reason for absence.

The director emphasized that student success relies on a collective effort from teachers, parents, and school administrators. He pointed out that even with free support sessions at his school, a lack of consistent student participation hinders their effectiveness. Some students' parents are called in, but the same excuses for absence are often repeated.

gn.headline: FIM board reviews budget execution
gn.dek: Guinea's Mining Investment Fund faces delays in public procurement processes, impacting project timelines.
paragraphs: The Mining Investment Fund (FIM) held its 10th ordinary board meeting in Conakry on Thursday, November 5, 2026. Participants reviewed the activity report up to August 31, 2026, and discussed a budget revision following the adoption of the amended Finance Law.

Aboubacar Kagbè Touré, the board chairman, noted progress in resource mobilization for 2025 and 2026 and overall spending control. However, he highlighted a low budget execution rate, attributing the delays to slow public procurement procedures.

Touré urged the general directorate to work with technical services to speed up the finalization of pending dossiers. He stressed that a budget's performance is measured by its absorption capacity, while also defending the need for legal compliance in disbursements.

gw.headline: US-funded vaccine trial cancelled in Guinea-Bissau
gw.dek: Accusations of unethical and neocolonial practices led to the cancellation of a hepatitis B vaccine trial on newborns.
paragraphs: A planned US-funded trial of a hepatitis B vaccine on newborn babies in Guinea-Bissau has been cancelled. Police seized a batch of vaccines from the Bandim Health Project research centre, which has operated in the country since 1978. The trial faced accusations of being unethical and neocolonial.

The proposed study drew international criticism for planning to withhold a World Health Organization-recommended vaccine from half of the participating newborns. Some public health experts questioned whether vulnerable populations in African countries were being subjected to risks not accepted in wealthier nations. The US Health Secretary, Robert F Kennedy Jr, who has expressed scepticism about vaccines, funded the trial.

Guinea-Bissau, like neighbouring countries, typically waits until babies are six weeks old for hepatitis B vaccinations, while the WHO recommends vaccination at birth. The BBC has sought comment from the US department of health and human services regarding the cancelled trial.

gw.headline: Guinea-Bissau admits UEMOA reform implementation lag
gw.dek: The Secretary of State for the Treasury noted a decline in implementing UEMOA policies compared to 2024.
paragraphs: Guinea-Bissau's Secretary of State for the Treasury, Justino Vieira, stated on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, that the country experienced a slight setback in implementing reforms, policies, programs, and community projects of the West African Economic and Monetary Union (UEMOA). This assessment follows the results of the latest Annual Technical Inspection.

Vieira acknowledged that the achieved results were unsatisfactory when compared to those from 2024, emphasizing the need for better coordination between national authorities and technical departments involved in transposing UEMOA directives. The evaluation, taking place in Bissau from November 4 to 6, aims to assess reform execution and identify solutions to strengthen national ownership of the sub-regional organization's policies.

The government intends to improve the implementation of UEMOA additional acts, regulations, and decisions, and accelerate the transposition of directives within set deadlines. Aly Coulibaly, the UEMOA Commission's resident representative in Guinea-Bissau, mentioned that the 2026 evaluation modalities were defined during preparatory work in Bamako, Mali, from June 22 to 26.

gw.dek: Federico Bianchi called for stronger environmental protection on Poilão, a key nesting site for marine turtles in West Africa.
paragraphs: The European Union representative in Guinea-Bissau, Federico Bianchi, asked the government to increase environmental protection on Poilão island. This island in the Bijagós Archipelago is a fundamental area for marine turtle reproduction in West Africa.

Bianchi spoke on Tuesday, November 3, 2026, during a beach cleanup event organised by the EU. He stated that plastic waste threatens marine life, human health, tourism, and the local economy. Poilão was chosen for the event because it is sacred to the Bijagó people and one of the region's most important turtle nesting sites.

The EU representative highlighted the importance of preserving marine resources for Guinea-Bissau’s economy, noting that fishing is a main sector. The French and Spanish ambassadors, along with representatives from the World Bank and WHO, also attended the cleanup. The French ambassador noted Poilão's preservation is key to protecting the UNESCO World Heritage Bijagós Archipelago.

gw.headline: Guinea-Bissau ministry clarifies energy tariffs
gw.dek: The Natural Resources Ministry stated the Gambia River Basin Development Organization is not responsible for electricity prices.
paragraphs: Guinea-Bissau's Ministry of Natural Resources responded on Thursday, November 5, 2026, to criticisms from the Consumers Association of Goods and Services (ACOBES) regarding electricity prices. The ministry clarified that the Organization for the Development of the Gambia River Basin (OMVG) does not set the tariffs applied in Guinea-Bissau.

ACOBES Secretary-General Bambo Sanhá had called the current electricity costs "worrying" and argued there was no justification for maintaining them. The ministry explained in a statement that the OMVG's primary role is regional electrical interconnection, not the production, sale, or pricing of energy consumed domestically.

The electricity supplied to Guinea-Bissau comes from the Kaleta hydroelectric dam in Guinea-Conakry and is sold by Electricidade da Guiné (EDG) to EAGB. The ministry stressed that the price EAGB pays the supplier differs from the final consumer tariff, which is determined by national factors. The government urged ACOBES to consult relevant authorities before making public statements on the energy sector.

lr.headline: Liberia's economy grew 5.1 percent in 2025
lr.dek: Despite strong growth, more Liberians slipped into extreme poverty as jobs stalled in key sectors.
paragraphs: Liberia's economy expanded by 5.1 percent in 2025, the fastest rate in five years according to the World Bank. Export earnings surged by nearly 58 percent, driven by gold and iron ore. However, the number of Liberians living in extreme poverty rose from 34.6 percent in 2024 to 36.1 percent in 2025.

The economic growth was fueled by a 42 percent increase in iron ore production and a 17 percent rise in overall mining output. Sectors where most Liberians work, such as manufacturing and agriculture, saw declines or slowed growth. Agriculture, employing 39 percent of the workforce, grew only 2.6 percent, and farm labour productivity has fallen about 1.1 percent annually since 2014.

The World Bank report highlights that the government cannot reliably track the finances of its 62 state-owned entities. While food inflation decreased due to lower rice prices, non-food inflation climbed to 9.9 percent, impacting housing, healthcare, and services costs for urban workers.

lr.headline: Liberia port authority acts on shipping delays
lr.dek: National Port Authority announces direct Maersk shipping and extended operations to ease congestion and rising fees.
paragraphs: Liberia's National Port Authority (NPA) is implementing new measures to tackle severe congestion and lengthy cargo delays at the Freeport of Monrovia. NPA Managing Director Sekou A. Dukuly announced that shipping giant Maersk will now deliver vessels directly to Monrovia, bypassing transshipment through other West African ports. This move aims to reduce transit times and associated costs for Liberian importers who have protested mounting fees and prolonged delays.

Dukuly acknowledged the port's undercapacity, which has left approximately 700 containers stranded for over 30 days, creating significant financial strain on businesses. The NPA plans to clear these containers, suspend berth repairs to allow simultaneous vessel berthing, and extend working hours. The authority is also considering granting additional free days for importers facing demurrage and storage charges.

The NPA is exploring engagement with the Central Bank of Liberia and commercial banks to offer short-term financial relief to affected businesses. This could include easing loan repayment obligations for importers whose capital is tied up in delayed shipments. These proposals come after importers, many of whom secured business loans against personal property, reported threats to their operations due to accumulating costs and delays.

lr.dek: Dr. Isaac P. Podah says rapid enrollment growth strains finances, staff, and transport.
paragraphs: Lofa County University President Dr. Isaac P. Podah reported that the institution's rapid expansion is increasing access to higher education in rural Liberia but straining its finances, workforce, transportation, and infrastructure. Enrollment has surged from about 500-600 students two years ago to approximately 3,000 students across two campuses. Dr. Podah stated this growth requires stronger financial support to maintain operations and retain qualified lecturers.

Speaking at a workshop in Ganta, Dr. Podah explained that the university's annex in Fessibu Town, Zorzor District, was established to bring education closer to students facing financial and transport barriers to Voinjama. He identified budget constraints as the most pressing challenge, estimating that L$4 million is needed to manage operations. This funding pressure impacts staff compensation, transportation, and infrastructure.

The workshop, organized by the National Commission on Higher Education with UNDP support, focused on strengthening higher education governance and quality assurance. Leaders discussed governance, educational standards, and university development. Dr. Podah described the exchange as valuable for efforts to improve higher education in underserved areas.

lr.headline: Liberia health minister accused of ignoring Sinje center fraud
lr.dek: National Polit-Bureau of Liberia says Dr. Louise Kpoto failed to act on internal report detailing missing funds and drugs.
paragraphs: The National Polit-Bureau of Liberia (NPBL) accused Health Minister Dr. Louise M. Kpoto on Thursday, November 5, 2026, of ignoring financial and administrative problems at the Sinje Comprehensive Health Center in Grand Cape Mount County. NPBL National Chairman Victor L. Balo stated that an internal Ministry of Health investigation from June 3–6, 2026, documented LD$3,705,120 in unbanked revenue and a US$20,583.59 financial discrepancy. The report also noted the disappearance of 646 patient care tablets, procurement fraud, and excessive billing.

Balo criticized the minister for five months of silence following the investigation, warning that inaction could erode public confidence in healthcare. He specifically targeted Dr. Sampson Wulu, the center's Medical Director, for accountability. The NPBL also highlighted concerns about maternal deaths and poor childbirth outcomes, calling for an independent clinical review with international partners. The organization alleged that investigators who authored the report face potential sanctions.

The NPBL demanded a public explanation from Minister Kpoto, a forensic audit, financial reconciliation, and investigations into missing pharmaceuticals, procurement, and billing. They also called for administrative action against Dr. Wulu and protection for whistleblowers. The civil society group warned that administrative lapses expose pregnant women and vulnerable patients to preventable medical risks.

lr.headline: Liberia hosts customs meeting on cross-border crime
lr.dek: More than 40 delegates from 17 West and Central African nations met in Margibi County to enhance intelligence sharing.
paragraphs: Customs officials and intelligence officers from 17 West and Central African countries are meeting in Liberia to strengthen their fight against cross-border crime. The 17th Joint Annual Meeting of National Contact Points of the World Customs Organization Regional Intelligence Liaison Offices is being held at the Farmington Hotel in Margibi County. The Liberia Revenue Authority is hosting the weeklong forum, which focuses on improving intelligence sharing and coordinated enforcement against smuggling and other transnational crimes.

Amadou Tidiane Cisse, Director General of RILO West Africa, opened the meeting on Monday, calling it a critical platform for cooperation. He stated that sharing intelligence helps disrupt criminal networks involved in trafficking narcotics, counterfeit medicines, and protected wildlife. Liberia’s Commissioner of Customs, Saa Saamoi, highlighted the urgent need for stronger regional intelligence sharing and coordinated border enforcement, noting that criminal groups exploit system weaknesses.

Delegates will review recommendations from the previous meeting in Bamako, Mali, and examine issues related to intelligence exchange, data quality, and regional operations. They will also discuss the use of WCO Customs Enforcement Network platforms. The meeting aims to develop practical recommendations and establish follow-up mechanisms for implementing decisions.

ly.headline: Libyan publishers face rising book costs
ly.dek: Fluctuating exchange rates and import expenses drive up production costs for local books.
paragraphs: Libyan publishers are struggling with increased book production costs due to reliance on imported paper and fluctuating foreign currency exchange rates. These economic challenges are pushing up retail prices for books across the country.

Ali Jaber, manager of Al-Jaber Publishing, stated that printing costs are similar across Libya, Egypt, and Tunisia because all presses use imported paper. He explained that books are often priced using the US dollar on the parallel market, as official letters of credit for imports are unavailable, making production costs dependent on unofficial exchange rates. In 2010, producing a book cost about $5, equivalent to 7.5 dinars, but today the same dollar amount is nearly 50 dinars.

While Libyan titles typically range from 30 to 50 dinars, imported books can cost 100 to 1000 dinars. Shipping books from Cairo to Benghazi can be cheaper than between some Libyan cities, costing about 100 dinars per parcel, though delays of up to 45 days are common. Printing in Egypt offers Libyan publishers more flexibility for participating in international book fairs.

ly.headline: Libya seizes 21 trucks carrying subsidised goods
ly.dek: 15 trucks were found heading towards border regions, suspected of being used for smuggling.
paragraphs: Libyan authorities intercepted 21 trucks and their drivers on Monday, November 2, for allegedly transporting subsidised goods. The Anti-Financial Crimes, Money Laundering, and Terrorist Financing (AFCMLTF) reported that six trucks were released after initial checks, but 15 were found to be heading towards border areas.

These 15 trucks, along with their drivers, were referred to the AFCMLTF for legal proceedings. Investigators suspect these domestic transport operations are a front for smuggling goods out of the country. The case file was sent to the Advocate General in Tripoli for further action.

The operation follows directives from the Prime Minister to control rising prices of essential commodities. Measures include increased oversight on transport, distribution, and storage to ensure goods remain in local markets and prices are stable.

ly.headline: Malta firm discusses marine safety centre in Tripoli
ly.dek: Camilleri Marine director visited the Libyan Ports Company to advance plans for a new maintenance facility.
paragraphs: Kenneth Camilleri, director of Malta-based Camilleri Marine, visited the Libyan Ports Company's branch at the Port of Tripoli yesterday. The visit aimed to establish a specialized centre for maintaining marine vessels' safety equipment.

Camilleri toured the "Oea Marine Centre," slated to open soon, and discussed operational mechanisms and a memorandum of understanding with Libyan Ports Company officials. The centre, designed to international standards, will enhance technical services for marine safety equipment.

An agreement was reached on executive steps to accelerate preparations for the "Oea Marine Centre," Libya's first facility of its kind. This centre will begin operations after technical procedures and equipment installation are complete.

ly.headline: Libya cuts customs dollar rate to LD 2.12
ly.dek: The Ministry of Finance reduced the rate used for import duties from LD 4.80 to LD 2.12 per US dollar.
paragraphs: Libya's Ministry of Finance issued a directive last Tuesday, November 3, to lower the Customs Dollar exchange rate for imported goods. The rate has been set at 2.12 Libyan dinars per US dollar, a significant decrease from the previous rate of 4.80 Libyan dinars.

This temporary measure, announced via official directive, aims to adjust the calculation of duties on imported goods. The Ministry of Finance stated this change is pending the resolution of existing issues related to the rate.
The directive suspends Resolution No. (160) of 2026, which previously governed the Customs Dollar exchange rate. This adjustment impacts the cost of importing goods into Libya.

mg.headline: Tendry Rakotobe sets new Madagascar swimming record
mg.dek: The young swimmer finished ninth overall in the 50m backstroke at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympics.
paragraphs: Madagascar swimmer Tendry Rakotobe set a new national record in the 50m backstroke at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympics. He finished fourth in his heat with a time of 27.35 seconds, placing him ninth overall and narrowly missing a spot in the final.

Rakotobe's performance surpassed his previous personal best of 27.7 seconds, established two years ago. His teammate Océane Rakotonanahary competed in the 50m breaststroke, finishing fourth in her heat in 34.65 seconds and eleventh overall.
Two other Malagasy athletes are still competing: Francia Nomenjanahary Randriatiana in beach wrestling on November 8 and Jauslin Anjara Laura in the 200m athletics sprint on November 10.

mg.headline: Madagascar suspends Boeing 777 trial for new probe
mg.dek: The anti-corruption court suspended the trial of 38 people linked to the transfer of five Boeing 777s to Iran, sending it back for further investigation.
paragraphs: The trial concerning five Boeing 777 aircraft sent to Iran has been suspended by Madagascar's Anti-Corruption Pole (PAC) without a new date. The case returns to the investigative stage at the request of the prosecution, which deems further investigations necessary. This decision prolongs the uncertainty for the 38 individuals prosecuted.

The dean of investigative judges will resume investigations, examining new elements including complaints from the new management of the Civil Aviation of Madagascar (ACM), reports from the Independent Anti-Corruption Bureau (Bianco), and technical expertise from American specialists. These documents aim to clarify responsibilities in the administrative authorizations granted for the aircraft transfer.

The case, which erupted in July 2025, also faces a potential reclassification of offenses to criminal infractions, which would significantly alter the procedure. Former Transport Minister Valéry Ramonjavelo and former Senate President General Richard Ravalomanana are among those implicated in the affair.

mg.headline: ORTM director clashes with communication minister over access
mg.dek: A dispute over security measures at public broadcasting premises escalates between the ORTM director general and the communication minister.
paragraphs: A dispute has erupted between the director general of the Office de la Radio et de la Télévision de Madagascar (ORTM), Lemana Elysée, and the Minister of Communication and Culture, Gascar Fenosoa, over access to the Havoria hall within the ORTM compound in Anosy. The conflict escalated on Wednesday evening when the ministry attempted to implement new access controls, leading to a confrontation that required the intervention of the Organe mixte de conception (OMC).

The disagreement stems from ORTM's decision to restrict access to Havoria, citing security concerns due to its shared premises with the national radio and television buildings, which are classified as red zones. The ORTM director general reportedly closed a connecting gate and increased security checks, disrupting events and causing cancellations. The ministry responded by installing metal barriers to separate the sites and reopen access to Havoria, a move the ORTM director allegedly opposed and dismantled.

Further complicating the situation, the ORTM management has reportedly given ministry services occupying ORTM offices one week to vacate the premises. These services include the Directorate of Public Relations and the regional communication directorate. The minister and the head of the OMC were present to oversee the barrier installation, while the ORTM director general allegedly called in Presidential Security elements during the standoff.

mw.headline: Activist disputes NGO regulator's power to deregister HRDC
mw.dek: Veteran activist Redson Munlo argues the Non-Governmental Organisations Regulatory Authority (NGORA) lacks legal authority to deregister the Human Rights Defenders Coalition.
paragraphs: Veteran activist Redson Munlo has challenged the Non-Governmental Organisations Regulatory Authority's (NGORA) move to deregister the Human Rights Defenders Coalition (HRDC). Munlo stated that civil society organisations are not legally required to register with NGORA, therefore the body cannot deregister them.

Munlo described NGORA as an association without regulatory powers over independent civil society groups. He noted that many prominent organisations in Malawi’s civic space operate without being NGORA members and continue their work. This dispute could concern international donors monitoring Malawi's democratic standing.

Development partners, including the European Union, the United Kingdom, and UN agencies, rely on groups like HRDC to monitor transparency and public funds. NGORA announced the revocation of HRDC's status, citing operational shortcomings.

mw.headline: Malawi plane crash evidence vanishes
mw.dek: Forensic samples and photographs from the June 10, 2024 crash that killed Saulos Chilima are missing.
paragraphs: Forensic samples and photographs from the June 10, 2024 plane crash that killed former vice-president Saulos Chilima and eight others have disappeared. Senior medical officer Andrew Master Mwale told the plane crash enquiry that samples he collected and stored at Sun Set Funeral Services could no longer be traced. The missing evidence raises serious questions about the investigation's transparency and completeness.

Mwale expressed surprise that materials from such a sensitive investigation could go missing without explanation. He noted that eight bodies were kept at Sun Set Funeral Services, which had reportedly inadequate security compared to Goodwill Funeral Services, where Chilima's body was held. The disappearance of photographs taken during recovery and postmortems also hinders independent specialists from reconstructing the process and verifying forensic observations.

Substantial human tissue, including muscle and backbone fragments, was recovered, but some materials, including a large tissue sample believed to belong to Abdul Lapukeni, remain unaccounted for. Questions also surround the identification of body parts attributed to Chilima, specifically an amputated leg and foot. Mwale stated that independent DNA testing, potentially in South Africa or Zambia, is increasingly important to confirm victim identities.

mw.headline: Malawi council launches K3.6 billion development projects
mw.dek: Lilongwe City Council's Reformed Constituency Development Fund package includes a health facility, secondary school, and road improvements.
paragraphs: Lilongwe City Council has launched K3.6 billion in development projects for the Mtandire-Mtsiriza constituency, aiming to improve lives within five months. The Reformed Constituency Development Fund (RCDF) package includes a new health facility, a secondary school, and infrastructure upgrades like box culverts and drainage to combat flooding. Besphat Construction Company, Fukumule Construction, and Lukam Construction Company will carry out the work.

Member of Parliament Alfred Gangata stated that residents identified the projects to meet their development needs and urged community ownership. ml.headline: Mali signs two geological accords with Russia
ml.dek: The agreements aim to create a digital geological map and a national information system.
paragraphs: Mali signed two geological cooperation agreements with Russia on October 29, 2026, on the sidelines of the Russia-Africa summit in Moscow. The accords were signed between Mali's Ministry of Mines and Zarubezhgeologia, a subsidiary of the Russian state-owned Rosgeologia group.

The first agreement focuses on creating a digital geological map covering over half of Mali's territory. The second establishes a national information system to centralize geological data, aid analysis, and manage mining licenses and activities. These agreements also include training for Malian specialists in interpreting satellite imagery.

The accords aim to improve the understanding and management of Mali's resources. They do not constitute the granting of new exploitation permits or the announcement of commercially viable discoveries. The summit itself covered a broad economic agenda, including cereals, nuclear energy, education, and trade routes.

ml.headline: Mali seeks climate adaptation funds at COP31
ml.dek: The nation aims to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 25.25% by 2035, but needs financial backing for adaptation projects.
paragraphs: Mali is seeking international climate finance at COP31 in Antalya, Turkey, from November 9 to 20. The country aims to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 25.25% by 2035 and needs funds for adaptation projects to protect crops and water resources. Recent rainfall disruptions in Sikasso and Bougouni highlighted the vulnerability of agricultural activities to unpredictable weather patterns.

Gaoussou Berthé, an environmental expert, noted that political commitments have not always been matched by necessary funding for implementation. Mali presented its third-generation climate contribution on October 1, focusing on adaptation priorities alongside mitigation goals. The nation has previously mobilized resources, with the national climate fund financing over 30 projects worth more than 20 billion CFA francs by April 2026.

Dr. Ibrahim Togola, President of Réso-Climat Mali, stated that developing countries often lack the financial resources and technical knowledge to address climate emergencies. He emphasized the importance of solutions like improved seeds, agricultural insurance, and better weather forecasts for farmers. International climate finance goals include at least $300 billion annually by 2035 for developing countries and tripling adaptation finance by the same year.

ml.headline: Mali religious leaders tackle extremism
ml.dek: The Bamako document proposes religious leaders help prevent violent extremism through training and community outreach.
paragraphs: Mali's Prime Minister Abdoulaye Maïga received the "Bamako Document for the deconstruction of extremist discourse in Mali" on October 29. The High Islamic Council-backed document aims to leverage religious leaders' influence to counter violent extremism. Diakité Kadia Togola, President of the National Union of Muslim Women's Associations of Mali, expressed concern for the youth's future, aligning with the document's goals.

The government plans to use religious figures' proximity to communities to combat religiously justified violence. This initiative follows a July 16, 2026, request from the Ministry of Religious Affairs to the High Islamic Council to create a reference document against hate speech. The national policy against extremism, launched in 2018 with an action plan ending in 2026, supports these efforts.

Previous initiatives show potential for community engagement. A UNDP report from April 2023 detailed the PARLER project, which trained 120 religious actors in sermon guidance in areas like Bla and Koutiala. Aïssata Coumaré, a medersa teacher in Koutiala, noted improved understanding of social cohesion. The program also involved 27 radio stations and prepared social media messages. Separately, 80 Imams were offered places at the Mohammed VI Institute in Rabat on August 22, 2026, for training in preventing extremism.

mr.headline: Three Koumé family members to face Nouakchott court
mr.dek: Family members protest forced eviction and arrest, announcing a sit-in for November 5.
paragraphs: Three young members of the Koumé family will appear before the Nouakchott west prosecutor on Thursday, November 5, 2026, following their arrest during a controversial eviction from their home on Îlot L in the capital. The family claims the eviction on October 21 involved nine police vehicles and disputes the land documents used for the operation.

The family's relatives are demanding the immediate release of the three youths and have called for a peaceful sit-in outside the Nouakchott west Palace of Justice if they are not freed before their court appearance. The Koumé family states that women and children are still living on the street opposite their former residence and reports death threats against some members on November 3.

The organizers of the planned sit-in are calling for the family's return to their home, an independent investigation into the eviction and arrests, and accountability for those responsible. They are inviting human rights organizations, lawyers, civil society associations, media, and citizens to join the gathering to demand justice and protection for the Koumé family.

mu.headline: Woman shot in neck leaves hospital
mu.dek: Élodie Thomas, 27, returns home after a month of hospital care for a gunshot wound.
paragraphs: Élodie Thomas, 27, left ENT Hospital for home on Friday, November 6, almost a month after being shot in the neck. The young mother was injured on October 9 while returning from work at Winners supermarket. She underwent a seven-hour surgery at Dr. A. G. Jeetoo Hospital to remove the bullet.

A team of 13 foreign specialists cared for Thomas. She can now walk again and is reunited with her family, though she remains under strict medical supervision. Her husband, Jonathan, is with her as she begins her recovery. Investigators continue to question Sergeant Gowtamsing Taukoor, who is suspected of firing the shot.
Sergeant Taukoor faces two provisional charges: "using firearm to intimidate" and "involuntary wounds and blows by imprudence." Health Minister Anil Bachoo confirmed Thomas's 90% recovery.

mu.headline: Mauritius police arrest second murder suspect
mu.dek: Ridwaan Bauluck, 34, detained in connection with the killing of Selven Iyempermal on October 27.
paragraphs: The Major Crime Investigation Team (MCIT) arrested Ridwaan Bauluck, 34, on Thursday, November 5, as a second suspect in the murder of Selven Iyempermal. The victim was attacked by masked men with sabres and sticks in La Caverne, Vacoas, on the evening of Tuesday, October 27, and died from his injuries the next day. Police are investigating the motive as a possible settling of scores, with the victim suspected of involvement in drug trafficking in the area.

Bauluck, a father of one, denied involvement during questioning by the MCIT, stating he was at home with family. Investigators are verifying his alibi, and a relative is expected to be interviewed. He was placed under arrest and spent the night in a cell before appearing in court on Friday, November 6, for a provisional charge.

This arrest follows the apprehension of a first suspect, Imtiyaz Chady, 35, who has been in detention since October 30. The MCIT had previously conducted a police raid at the detoxification center in Vacoas as part of the ongoing investigation into Iyempermal's death.

CEO Kevin Ramkaloan highlighted initiatives since 2019 to promote efficient water use, including the creation of the Water Stewardship Forum in 2023.

mu.headline: CEB prepares for Divali power demand surge
mu.dek: The Central Electricity Board is deploying special teams and urging consumer caution to ensure uninterrupted electricity supply during the festival.
paragraphs: The Central Electricity Board (CEB) is activating special measures to manage an anticipated increase in electricity demand during Divali. The CEB announced on October 30 that its technical teams will be on standby to respond swiftly to any power outages, ensuring a continuous supply for the festival.

The CEB is advising consumers to use electrical installations prudently, warning against overloading circuits and advising against self-manipulation of wiring. They also recommend checking festive lights for damage and limiting the simultaneous use of high-consumption appliances like electric showers, kettles, and air conditioners when decorative lighting is active.

Customers experiencing power failures or supply issues are instructed to contact the CEB service at 130. The board's preparedness aims to prevent disruptions during the period of heightened electricity usage associated with Divali celebrations.

mu.headline: French surgeon completes second Mauritius mission
mu.dek: Dr Bruno Zipoli consulted 80 patients and performed 15 major surgeries at Jeetoo Hospital.
paragraphs: French orthopedic surgeon Dr Bruno Zipoli has completed his second medical mission at Dr A. G. Jeetoo Hospital in Port-Louis, Mauritius. The specialist conducted consultations and performed surgeries for complex orthopedic conditions from the week of November 2, 2026. This initiative aims to enhance local access to specialized surgical care and foster expertise sharing with Mauritian medical staff.

mz.headline: Mozambique bridge collapses again after repairs
mz.dek: A temporary Revuè River bridge in Manica province failed six days after reopening, disrupting traffic.
paragraphs: President Daniel Chapo announced plans for over $7.5bn in investments for Mozambique's Maputo, Beira, and Nacala transport corridors on Wednesday. The same day, a temporary metal bridge over the Revuè River in Manica province collapsed again. The bridge, on the road between Chimoio and Sussundenga, failed after a truck carrying sand or stones crossed it, disrupting traffic for the second time in a week.

The bridge had reopened only six days prior to the collapse. It is unclear if the truck exceeded the bridge's 30-tonne weight limit. This incident highlights ongoing issues with Mozambique's infrastructure management, where temporary emergency bridges are often used long past their intended lifespan.

The N1, the country's main north-south highway, also suffers from poor conditions on many sections. A $400m World Bank rehabilitation program for the N1 has been discussed for years, but significant improvements are still needed.
